_note: Official-source research behind the "Permits" and "Water, sod and sprinkler rules" sections on public/service-area/*.html and the town-by-town cards on the service pages (lib/service-town-rules.js). Every fact links to the city, town, county or water-provider page it came from. Watering rules change with drought stages: re-check before each spring and fall.

permit_office.name: City of Brighton Community Development – Building Division (One Stop permit counter)
permit_office.note: Permits and contractor licenses are applied for through the City's OpenGov portal; the One Stop counter (1stop@brightonco.gov, 303-655-2017) also handles right-of-way and utility permits.

row_permit.summary: Concrete work in the street right-of-way (such as curb, gutter, sidewalk or a driveway approach) needs a Right-of-Way permit through the One Stop permit counter before work starts, and the contractor must hold a City of Brighton contractor's license. The permit requires a traffic control plan, a site plan and a bond (at least $5,000 for repair/replace work, or 115% of job value above $4,348), and the contractor must give 24 hours' notice for inspection before concrete is placed.

retaining_wall.summary: Brighton's 'Do I Need a Building Permit?' handout (2021 IRC) says retaining walls not over 4 feet tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, do not need a building permit. Taller walls are not on the exempt list.

water_provider.name: City of Brighton Utilities Department (Water)

watering_rules.summary: Stage 1 drought restrictions (approved April 7, 2026, extended through Nov. 15, 2026) limit irrigation to two days a week: even addresses Tuesday and Friday, odd addresses Wednesday and Saturday, and unassigned HOA/landscape tracts Monday and Friday. Irrigation is banned 10 a.m.–6 p.m., water may not pool in gutters or streets, and hand watering with a hose held in the hand or a watering can is allowed.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 approved April 7, 2026; extended through Nov. 15, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Through Sept. 30, 2026, installing or replacing sod on areas over 200 sq ft was banned; starting Oct. 1, 2026, the City issues free sod permits (apply through OpenGov). Permit schedule: up to 3 waterings a day in weeks 1–2, twice a day in weeks 3–4 and once a day in weeks 5–6, with no watering 10 a.m.–6 p.m. after week 2, each watering 10 minutes or less, and normal restrictions after six weeks.

rebates.summary: Residential customers get $1 per sq ft of turf removed, up to $1,000. The design must be approved before work starts, have 70% native plant coverage and include no artificial turf; new builds and first-time landscaping are not eligible.
Rebate of 30% of the cost of an eligible WaterSense smart (ET) irrigation controller, one per customer.
Brighton Utilities customers can get a limited number of $25 discounts on Resource Central xeric garden kits; 2026 sales opened March 11.

backflow.summary: Residential irrigation systems must be protected from backflow, either isolated from household plumbing or with a containment assembly if on a separate service line, and containment assemblies must be tested annually with reports sent to the City. Testers must send passing reports to Brighton Utilities (backflow@brightonco.gov) within 10 business days and report failed tests within 24 hours.

other.summary: Repairing the sidewalk, curb and gutter is the abutting property owner's responsibility (Municipal Code 12-8-20), and replacements must meet City standards and be done by a licensed, insured and bonded contractor. The City's 50/50 program pays half of sidewalk, curb and gutter replacement while funds last, but does not cover driveways or concrete on private property.

permit_office.name: City of Commerce City Building Safety Division
permit_office.note: Building Safety: 303-289-3790, cdpermits@c3gov.com, Civic Center, 7190 Colorado Blvd Ste 600.

row_permit.summary: Work in the public right-of-way needs a Right-of-Way (ROW) permit from Commerce City Public Works. All contractors must pull the permit and first get a Commerce City contractor's license with a certificate of insurance; apply through eTRAKiT at least one week ahead, and schedule inspections 24 hours in advance.

flatwork_permit.summary: Driveways and on-grade patios (including wood patios) are on the City's list of projects exempt from a building permit. Exempt projects must still meet building code and planning setback rules.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 4 feet need a building permit. Walls 4 feet and under (measured from top of wall to bottom of footing) that do not support a surcharge are exempt.

water_provider.name: South Adams County Water & Sanitation District (SACWSD)
water_provider.note: The City states that water in Commerce City is provided by SACWSD, a separate special district, and that the city government does not provide water.

watering_rules.summary: SACWSD declared a Stage 1 drought on May 13, 2026, limiting watering to two days a week: single-family odd addresses Wednesday and Saturday, even addresses Sunday and Thursday, and multifamily/commercial Tuesday and Friday. Outdoor watering is banned 10 a.m.–6 p.m. year-round; flowers and vegetables may be hand-watered with a shut-off hose any day, and residential fines are $100, $250, then $500 after a warning.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (SACWSD Stage 1 declared May 13, 2026)

new_sod.summary: During Stage 1, new sod or seed may be watered for no more than 21 consecutive days, then no more than two days a week on the assigned schedule. SACWSD strongly discourages new sod June–August, lists April, May, September or October for new sod, and asks installers to notify it through its New Sod & Seed Installation form.

rebates.program: Garden In A Box discount (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Commerce City residents get $25 off Resource Central low-water garden kits (kits from $132) through the City's Energy, Equity and Environment Division; 2026 discounts opened March 11, with pickup in May or June.

backflow.summary: SACWSD rules require backflow assemblies that CDPHE requires to be controlled, including irrigation assemblies, to be tested by a certified technician by Aug. 31 each year, with reports sent to the District (backflowreports@sacwsd.org); the District's backflow page describes annual testing as a requirement for commercial customers. Irrigation lines in new construction generally need a pressure vacuum breaker or reduced-pressure assembly, and atmospheric vacuum breakers are not allowed on irrigation systems.

other.summary: Property owners must keep the sidewalk next to their property maintained and hazard-free (City Code Sec. 6-2012). The City's 2026 Sidewalk Repair Program splits eligible public-sidewalk repairs 50/50; applications are closed and reopen in 2027.

permit_office.name: City of Thornton Building Inspection Division (City Development – Building Division)
permit_office.note: Apply through the CityView Portal; 303-538-7250, buildings@thorntonco.gov, 9500 Civic Center Dr.

row_permit.summary: Work in Thornton's public right-of-way needs an Infrastructure Right-of-Way construction permit from Public Works Engineering Services. These permits go only to contractors with a Thornton contractor license, are applied for online at permits.thorntonco.gov (about 14 business days' review, plus a traffic control permit) and require a pre-construction meeting at least 48 hours before work. Cut sidewalk must be replaced by the full panel, and the page says the City does not allow curb cuts because no ADA-compliant specifications are approved.

flatwork_permit.summary: Concrete sidewalks on private property and concrete porches without roofs do not need a building permit. New residential driveway permits have been filed with the Planning & Zoning Division since Oct. 28, 2024, through the CityView portal ('Apply for a Planning Permit').

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 48 inches from the bottom of the footing need a building permit, with engineering required. Walls 48 inches or less that do not support a surcharge are exempt, and retaining walls qualify for the Building Division's homeowner rapid review.

water_provider.name: City of Thornton (Thornton Water, Infrastructure Department)
water_provider.note: The City's drought permit form says the permit is only for Thornton water customers and tells sewer-only customers to contact their water provider, so some properties with Thornton sewer service get water from another provider.

watering_rules.summary: Stage 1 drought (effective March 15, 2026) limits lawn watering to two days a week, and customers choose their two days; lawn watering is banned 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Trees, shrubs, perennials, annuals and vegetable gardens may be watered any day, and lawn watering under Stage 1 rules continues in October.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 effective March 15, 2026; page last modified Sept. 28, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Thornton discourages new sod or seed during the drought. A Drought Irrigation Permit allows extra watering for 21 days for new sod or seed ($50) or 42 days for native/warm-season grass seed ($100); permits are offered for May, June, September and October installs (none for July or August) and only to Thornton water customers.

rebates.summary: Up to $2 per sq ft for converting grass or a problem area to a low-water garden (2026 rules); all-rock projects with no plants do not qualify.

Remove at least 200 sq ft of lawn: the 2026 removal service is $2.75 per sq ft, with the City paying the first $1.75 per sq ft up to $750. The DIY option (up to 4 free Garden In A Box kits) filled for 2026.
Up to $200 for a WaterSense-certified, weather-based, Wi-Fi irrigation controller, one per 10 years.
$25 for a residential rain sensor connected to a sprinkler system, one per 10 years.
A 2026 residential artificial turf rebate is offered; the amount and rules are in the City's 2026 rules document.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluation (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free sprinkler evaluation with a custom watering schedule for Thornton Water customers; the 2026 program is full and a 2027 interest list is open.
Limited Thornton discounts on Resource Central low-water garden kits, sold in early spring and late summer while supplies last.

backflow.summary: Installing a backflow preventer for a new lawn sprinkler system needs a building permit, issued without plan review. Thornton's program requires backflow assemblies to be tested by a certified technician at installation and at least yearly, with results filed online through Backflow Solutions Inc. (BSI Online); the city describes the annual-inspection requirement for commercial, industrial and multifamily (3+ unit) properties.

other.summary: The City's Concrete Replacement Program ($140,000 a year) replaces broken or damaged concrete, prioritized by pedestrian hazard, structural damage, surface wear and drainage impact; work generally starts in March.

permit_office.name: City of Northglenn Building Division (building services provided by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.note: The Building Division is in City Hall, 11701 Community Center Dr.; call 303-450-8745 to reach the SAFEbuilt representative.

row_permit.summary: Any work by a private company on City-owned or controlled ground (streets, sidewalks, medians, easements) needs a Right-of-Way permit from Public Works' Right-of-Way Division (row@northglenn.org), applied for online with contractor registration and a bond; public sidewalk or curb-and-gutter replacement is also listed as permit work handled by Public Works. Concrete replacement in the right-of-way requires an approved traffic control plan, form inspections with 24 hours' notice, and soils testing before the pour.

flatwork_permit.summary: Concrete private sidewalks and driveways and concrete or stone patio slabs without roofs do not need a building permit. Public sidewalk or curb-and-gutter replacement does need a permit, through Public Works.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls 4 feet or more, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, need a building permit.

water_provider.name: City of Northglenn water utility (Public Works / Water Resources)

watering_rules.summary: Stage 2 mandatory restrictions: odd addresses water Wednesday and Saturday, even addresses Thursday and Sunday, and multifamily, commercial, HOA and park properties Tuesday and Friday, with no lawn watering on Mondays; lawn irrigation is allowed only 6 p.m.–10 a.m. Maximum run times per zone apply (for example, in July: 24 minutes for fixed spray, 52 for rotor, 65 for rotary heads), and trees, shrubs and gardens may be watered any time by shut-off hose, can or drip.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 2; 2026 rules dated April 14, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Under the 2026 rules, new sod or seed is allowed only on newly developed commercial properties and residential properties never landscaped before, with limited exceptions by application. A free permit allows watering new sod for up to 21 days, applied for before installation with the sod/seed receipt; sod repairs under 16 sq ft may be hand-watered any time.

rebates.summary: Up to $100 for a WaterSense-labeled irrigation timer, one per address every 10 years (Northglenn water customers; credited to the water bill).
$3 per rotary sprinkler head, up to 25 per address.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow & Smart Controller Program (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free irrigation checkup; participants may also qualify for a free Rachio smart controller and Rain Bird rain sensor (call 303-999-3824).
Lawn removal service discounted up to $750, or a DIY option with up to 4 Garden In A Box kits at no cost.
$25 discount for Northglenn residents on xeriscape garden kits; sales open in March and June.

backflow.summary: A building permit is needed when a lawn sprinkler backflow device is installed or replaced, and the City generally requires reduced-pressure (RP) backflow assemblies on irrigation lines, with some exceptions. Annual testing by an ABPA- or ASSE-certified tester is required for commercial, industrial and non-single-family residences, with reports filed through BSIonline.com.

other.summary: Call 811 (Colorado 811/UNCC) before digging to have City water and sewer lines and other utilities marked; except in emergencies, allow 48 hours for the response.
Contractors hired by a homeowner must be licensed with the City and pull the permits; homeowners permitting work on their own dwelling do not need a contractor's license.

permit_office.name: City of Federal Heights Building Department
permit_office.note: Electrical permits and inspections in Federal Heights are handled by the State (DORA).

row_permit.summary: Sidewalk, curb/gutter, driveway cut ('drivecut'), street cut and utility work in the right-of-way needs a Public Works/Engineering permit from the City's Engineering/Public Works Department. A traffic plan is required for all work in streets or rights-of-way, all work is subject to inspection, and the permit is void if work does not start within 30 days.

flatwork_permit.summary: Concrete sidewalks on private property and concrete porches without roofs are on the Building Department's list of projects that do not need a building permit (revised Sept. 13, 2023).

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 36 inches from the bottom of the footing need a building permit, and engineering is required.

water_provider.name: City of Federal Heights water utility (water purchased from the City of Westminster)
water_provider.note: Per the 2026 Water Quality Report, 100% of the water supplied in 2025 was treated surface water bought from Westminster (Standley Lake source).

watering_rules.summary: Federal Heights follows Westminster's Drought Management Plan and has been under a voluntary Drought Watch since April 15, 2026; mandatory watering restrictions are not in place. Residents are asked to water no more than 3 days a week and to water lawns before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Drought Watch effective April 15, 2026)

backflow.summary: The City's Backflow Prevention Program requires backflow prevention units and certified annual inspections for all businesses (Municipal Code Sec. 62-23); the page sets no testing schedule for single-family homes. Lawn sprinklers are on the City's list of projects that need a building permit.

other.summary: Streets and utilities inside Federal Heights mobile home parks are private; concerns there go to the park management office, not City Public Works.

permit_office.name: City of Westminster Building Division
permit_office.note: Permits are applied for through eTRAKiT; 303-658-2075, permits@westminsterco.gov, 4800 W 92nd Ave. Homeowners living in the home can apply for their own permits; hired contractors must be on the permit.

row_permit.summary: All work in the public right-of-way, including curb and gutter and sidewalks, needs a ROW permit reviewed by the Engineering Division and issued only to a contractor with a Class D Public Way Contractor's License ($10,000 letter-of-credit or cash surety plus insurance). Apply through eTRAKiT with a traffic control plan and a Colorado 811 locate confirmation number; fees include a $50 administrative fee, and unauthorized work is $500 per occurrence.

water_provider.name: City of Westminster water utility

watering_rules.summary: Westminster has been under a voluntary Drought Watch since April 15, 2026, and mandatory watering restrictions are not in place. Guidance is to water turf no more than three days a week and to water before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Drought Watch effective April 15, 2026)

rebates.summary: Free turf removal service and DIY options for Westminster residents through the City's Resource Central partnership.
Free sprinkler audit with a follow-up report.
Discounts on professionally designed, plant-by-number low-water garden kits.

rebates.program: HOA irrigation audits and turf-to-native conversion
rebates.summary: Programs for HOAs creating water-wise common areas, run through the Neighborhood Sustainability Program.

backflow.summary: Irrigation services must have an approved backflow prevention assembly (requirements for single- and multi-family homes are assessed based on site hazards), tested at installation and annually by a certified tester. Results go to the City's Cross-Connection Control team, submitted online through BSI Online (backflow@westminsterco.gov, 303-658-2477).

other.summary: The City notes that under state law HOAs cannot require a turf lawn, prohibit drought-tolerant (xeriscape) landscaping, or fine owners for brown landscaping during a drought.

permit_office.name: Town of Bennett Building Department (Community Development)
permit_office.note: Apply through the Town's SmartGov permit portal; 207 Muegge Way, 303-644-3249 ext. 1032, bennettbuilding@bennett.co.us.

row_permit.summary: A $75 Right-of-Way permit is needed for work in a Town right-of-way (street, sidewalk) or work that disrupts traffic: submit a site plan, traffic control plan and schedule, call 811, and notify Public Works 48 hours before starting (inspections can include forms/rebar and curb cuts). A separate $75 Access Permit is needed for a new driveway access point from a Town street or alley; access must be paved where it meets the right-of-way, with grades between 2% and 6%.

water_provider.name: Town of Bennett (Public Works) – groundwater wells
water_provider.note: The Town's 2026 Drinking Water Quality Report lists 11 groundwater wells in Adams County as the source.

watering_rules.summary: Standing rule: no watering 10 a.m.–6 p.m. (hand watering allowed). Mandatory Stage 1 restrictions took effect July 27, 2026, set to run through Sept. 8, 2026 unless modified: even addresses Monday/Wednesday/Friday, odd addresses Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday, a total of 4 watering hours per week, and no irrigation or hand watering 10 a.m.–6 p.m.
watering_rules.as_of: Stage 1 notice dated July 27, 2026 (in effect through Sept. 8, 2026 unless modified); standing rule adopted June 22, 2021

new_sod.summary: Residents who lay new seed or sod may apply to the Town for a special permit exempting them from the watering restrictions. The July 2026 Stage 1 notice also offers a temporary watering permit for new sod, seed or other qualifying landscaping.

other.summary: Installing or replacing artificial turf requires a $25 Artificial Turf Permit with a site plan showing slope and drainage and a base-prep inspection before installation; repairs do not need a permit.

The Town plans to raise water pressure in January 2027 when it moves to a single pressure zone, and offers a rebate of up to $550 for pressure reducing valves in eligible neighborhoods (Centennial, Brothers Four, Cordella, Old Town).
Permit fees double if work begins before the building permit is obtained.

permit_office.name: Town of Lochbuie Building Department (building services contracted to SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.note: Apply online through the CommunityConnect portal; contractors need a current Town license. Inspections are scheduled and performed by SAFEbuilt.

row_permit.summary: Lochbuie Public Works requires a Right-of-Way permit for work including curb, gutter, sidewalk and curb/driveway cuts, submitted online or to rowpermits@lochbuie.org. The form requires a one-year maintenance bond, 24 hours' notice before construction and Town inspection of all phases; there is a $150 application review fee plus permit fees, and all fees double if work starts without a permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Lochbuie Public Utilities
water_provider.note: The Town states it provides water, sewer and trash service to all Lochbuie residents.

watering_rules.summary: Effective June 1, 2026 until further notice: even addresses water Thursday and Sunday, odd addresses Wednesday and Saturday, HOA/metro district common areas Tuesday and Friday, and no watering on Monday; watering is banned 7 a.m.–9 p.m. and limited to 15 minutes per zone. The Town said outdoor watering would drop to one day a week starting in August if outdoor demand was not cut at least 5%.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (effective June 1, 2026, until further notice)

new_sod.summary: New lawns require a permit from Town Hall. Under Municipal Code Sec. 13-6-220 the permit (fee at least $20) allows watering once a day for up to 21 days for seeded lawns or 15 days for sod, up to 15 minutes per zone and not between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m.

backflow.summary: A lawn sprinkler system needs a One Stop building permit, and its site plan must show the backflow preventer location. No irrigation backflow testing schedule was found on the Town's site.

other.summary: Lochbuie's revised Public Works Standards and Specifications, which govern right-of-way construction, took effect May 30, 2026.

permit_office.name: City of Fort Lupton Building Department (Planning & Building). Applications go through the CommunityCore portal, and SAFEbuilt provides plan review and inspections.

row_permit.summary: Public Works issues these permits through Community Core. Any driveway repair or extension needs a "Public Works-Driveway Access" permit with a measured site plan. Work in the right-of-way needs a "Public Works - ROW" permit with a site plan and traffic control plan, including repair or replacement of sidewalks that run parallel to the street.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Building Department lists "concrete flat work inside property lines," concrete steps/ramps and decks/patios among the items that require a building permit, and its Q&A says a concrete patio needs a permit, with driveway and sidewalk permits coming from Public Works. General landscaping and sprinkler repairs do not need a building permit.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 4 feet tall require a building permit.

water_provider.name: City of Fort Lupton (Public Works water utility)
water_provider.summary: Some neighborhoods also have City non-potable irrigation systems, and the City's normal watering restrictions apply to them as well.

watering_rules.summary: From May 1 to September 30, 2026, no outdoor watering is allowed between 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. Residential car washing is limited to a bucket or a hose with a shut-off nozzle.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (May 1 to Sept. 30, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Residents planting new seed or sod lawns can apply for one 3-week watering waiver, which is required for both potable and non-potable irrigation systems. The permit is issued within 72 hours and must be displayed in a street-facing window.

backflow.summary: Homes with underground lawn irrigation must have an approved backflow (cross-connection control) device. A certified tester must test it before the system is turned on and every year after that, and submit the results to the City's program manager, Aqua Backflow (TrackMyBackflow.com). Lawn sprinkler systems also require a City permit.

other.summary: The City is responsible for sidewalks attached to the curb. Owners must repair and build detached sidewalks along their frontage, and a homeowner's sidewalk repair needs a permit from City Hall.
A residential driveway may cover up to 40% of the lot frontage or 27 feet, whichever is less. The water meter may not be paved over, and the main driveway must be concrete or asphalt.
In neighborhoods with City non-potable irrigation, homeowners may operate only their own purple-lid valve, not the City's meter pit or curb stop valve.

permit_office.name: Town of Hudson Building Permits & Inspections. Applications go through the CommunityCore portal, and the chief building official and inspection scheduling are provided through ProCode.

row_permit.summary: Public Works & Utilities requires a Right of Way Use/Access permit before trenching, utility work, road work, driveway cuts, culvert installation, boring or any other work in the right-of-way. A traffic control plan, bonding and insurance may be required, and processing averages 2 business days. Contractors making street cuts or excavations in the right-of-way must register with the Town, carry commercial liability insurance and post a bond warrantying the work for up to one year.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's permit guide exempts private sidewalks, walks and driveways that are no more than 30 inches above grade, are not over a basement and are not part of an accessible route. Excavations under 50 cubic yards are also exempt from permits.

retaining_wall.summary: A permit, with zoning and building review, is required for retaining walls over 4 feet tall measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall. Any wall that supports a surcharge or impounds Class I, II or IIIA liquids also needs a permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Hudson (Public Works & Utilities; utility billing at Town Hall)

backflow.summary: The Town's Water and Sewer design criteria (Vol. II, 2017) require a backflow assembly on any type of irrigation system: an air gap, AVB, PVB or RP depending on design. The Town Utilities Department must accept the assembly before installation, and it must be tested before the certificate of occupancy and retested every year.

other.summary: Public Works provides utility locates in response to 811 requests. The Town asks residents to call 811 a few days before any digging, even small jobs like tree planting or fence posts.
A lawn sprinkler system connected to potable water requires a building permit.

permit_office.name: Town of Keenesburg Building Department. The building official is provided by Charles Abbott Associates.

row_permit.summary: Any excavation or opening in a street, alley, sidewalk or other public right-of-way requires a Town Public Right of Way/Access (excavation) permit, including curb/gutter, sidewalk, driveway and access work. The work must be done by a bonded contractor with a certificate of insurance naming the Town, and Public Works needs 24 hours' notice for inspections.

water_provider.name: Town of Keenesburg (Public Works; the Town treats water from six wells)

backflow.summary: A residential lawn sprinkler backflow preventer is a one-stop building permit, and the Town fee schedule lists a $70 lawn sprinkler backflow preventer inspection. The Town's site does not publish a testing frequency.

other.summary: Temporary roll-off dumpsters are allowed with a no-fee permit for 15 days. They must be parked on the street, not on the driveway or sidewalk.

permit_office.name: City of Dacono Department of Community Development (Building Division). Building department services are contracted to SAFEbuilt Colorado, and permits go through Community Core.

row_permit.summary: An excavation permit from Public Works, Engineering and Water is required before making or changing sidewalks, driveways, curbs or gutters, or doing any other work on public property, easements or rights-of-way. The City's instructions list a $500 permit fee, a bond of $2,500 or $76 per square yard (whichever is greater) and liability insurance naming the City.

water_provider.name: City of Dacono (Department of Public Works, Engineering and Water)
water_provider.summary: The City supplies treated water to all customers within city limits. Central Weld County Water District treats that water and delivers it to the City.

watering_rules.summary: No mandatory watering restrictions are in place. The City asks residents to conserve voluntarily by checking irrigation systems for leaks and cutting a few minutes from each zone.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated page viewed Oct. 13, 2026 (references the City's 2026 Water Efficiency Plan)

new_sod.summary: On May 11, 2026 the City adopted a WaterWise Landscape Code (Ordinance No. 1016) that requires landscape and irrigation plans and limits turf grass.

backflow.summary: The City or its contractor performs annual backflow inspections at $100 per device, billed on the water bill. The program covers commercial, industrial, multifamily, HOA, fire and non-single-family irrigation services, and does not apply to single-family residential properties.

other.summary: Under its Sidewalk Repair Program, the City inspects and contracts repairs for damaged public sidewalks, such as vertical displacement over 3/4 inch or cracks over 1 inch wide. Residents can submit repair requests.
For 811 locates, the City marks only its water mains and the service line to the meter. Owners must locate their own service line from the meter to the house.

permit_office.name: Town of Frederick Building Department. Permit applications go through the Accela Citizen Access portal.

row_permit.summary: The Engineering Department requires a right-of-way permit for any work in the Town right-of-way, with a $150 non-refundable license fee plus a refundable deposit based on the amount of roadway cut. Applications are emailed and need a drawing of the work, a traffic control plan signed by an ATSSA-certified person and a work schedule, and Engineering schedules all inspections.

water_provider.name: Town of Frederick east of I-25; Left Hand Water District west of I-25
water_provider.summary: Three suppliers are involved in potable water within town limits: the Town, Central Weld County Water District and Left Hand Water District. All residents east of I-25 are Town customers, and residents west of I-25 are Left Hand Water District customers.

watering_rules.summary: On May 20, 2026 the Town declared a Stage 1 (Mild) Water Shortage for its customers east of I-25. It recommends no watering between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. and no more than three watering days per week, with voluntary compliance and a 10% reduction goal. Left Hand Water District, which serves Frederick west of I-25, has also declared a voluntary Stage 1.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 declared May 20, 2026)

new_sod.summary: The Town's 2026 Water Shortage Contingency Plan sets new-lawn (sod and seed) exceptions by permit. Stage 1 has no restrictions to exempt. In Stage 2, new lawns can be watered any day and time for the permitted period; in Stage 3 this applies only to September-to-April installations; Stages 4 and 5 allow no exceptions.

rebates.summary: Pays $2 per square foot, up to $2,000 per water account per year, for replacing at least 200 sq ft of lawn with low-water plantings or grasses; artificial turf is not eligible. Designs must be approved before work starts. 2026 projects had to be submitted Feb. 1 to Sept. 1 and completed and inspected by Oct. 20, 2026; open to Town water customers only.

Up to $200 utility-account credit for a new EPA WaterSense-certified Wi-Fi irrigation controller bought after Jan. 1, 2026, limited to one per household per 10 years. Open to Town water customers only; Left Hand Water District customers are referred to that district's rebates.
Town of Frederick water customers get a discount on Resource Central's waterwise perennial garden kits.
Free on-site sprinkler evaluation (about 75 minutes) and customized watering schedule from Resource Central for Town water customers.

backflow.summary: Irrigation, commercial, industrial and fire lines must have an approved backflow assembly, tested by a certified tester at installation and every year after. Results go to the Town and Aqua Backflow, and double-check assemblies are not allowed on irrigation systems. For single-family homes, requirements vary by hazard, and the Town encourages testing irrigation systems every three years.

other.summary: Since Nov. 16, 2024 the Land Use Code no longer requires turf in front yards. Front-yard landscaped areas must have at least 50% living plant cover rather than all rock or mulch, and existing properties do not have to change their landscaping.
Colorado 811 must be contacted at least three business days before any digging, fencing or construction, even on private property. Locates include oil and gas flowlines and gathering lines.

permit_office.name: Town of Firestone Building Division (Planning & Development Department). Permits go through the Citizenserve online portal.

row_permit.summary: The Engineering Division requires a Right of Way Permit before any work on or within Town property, right-of-way or easements, including street cuts, road closures, traffic control and installing utilities or improvements. The permit costs $200 plus fees and surety depending on the activity, and contractors must hold a Town of Firestone contractor license.

water_provider.name: Town of Firestone
water_provider.summary: The Town does not run its own treatment plant; it buys treated water from Central Weld County Water District and the St. Vrain Water Authority. Barefoot Lakes is served by Little Thompson Water District instead of the Town.

watering_rules.summary: Mandatory Stage 1 drought restrictions took effect April 16, 2026 and remain through the end of the year unless lifted. Even-numbered addresses may water Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday, and odd-numbered addresses Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday, with watering recommended between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (effective April 16, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Temporary watering permits (waivers) are available for lawns installed after April 1, 2026. Apply in person at the Town Hall utility billing counter (9950 Park Ave.) and post the permit where it is visible on the property.

rebates.summary: $750 discount on lawn removal services. The 2026 program is full and closed, and a 2027 interest list is open through Resource Central.

Free Wi-Fi smart irrigation controller (up to 8 zones, with rain/freeze sensor) for single-family Town water customers with at least one year of water use at the property. Not available for new construction, and the Town must inspect the installation within 30 days.
$25 discount on Resource Central waterwise garden kits for a limited number of Firestone residents (2026 collection).

backflow.summary: The Building Division's 2025 fee schedule lists a $100 permit for a residential backflow preventer ($225 for commercial). The Town's site does not publish a testing frequency.

other.summary: Artificial turf is allowed only in rear and side yards of single-family homes and needs a Town permit. It may cover at most 75% of that yard area, at least 25% must stay living landscape, a 3-foot living buffer is required at property lines, and it cannot go on slopes steeper than 5:1.

Barefoot Lakes customers of Little Thompson Water District are under a Water Shortage Watch as of April 2026. They may water only before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m., at most three days a week (even addresses Mon/Wed/Sat, odd addresses Tue/Thu/Sun), with fines starting at $100 on a second offense.

permit_office.name: Town of Erie Building Division (Planning & Development). Permits go through the eTRAKiT Self-Service Portal.

row_permit.summary: Work in the Town right-of-way needs a Right-of-Way Permit applied for through eTRAKiT, and every contractor working there must hold a Town of Erie contractor license. Review can take up to 10 business days, so apply at least two weeks ahead; the Town notes that work in the tree lawn also requires a ROW permit.

flatwork_permit.summary: Building permits are not required for concrete on-grade porches without roofs, concrete sidewalks on private property or general landscaping.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 4 feet, measured from the bottom of the trench to the top of the wall, require a building permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Erie (Water and Wastewater)
water_provider.summary: The Town's interactive map shows the providers for each address. The Town's drought plan notes that some properties in Erie's service area use wells or Left Hand Water District water.

watering_rules.summary: Stage 2 of the Town's drought plan asks customers to voluntarily water only two days a week: even-numbered addresses on Monday and Thursday, odd-numbered addresses on Tuesday and Friday. In extreme heat a third day may be announced by text alert (Saturday for even addresses, Sunday for odd). Stages 1 and 2 are voluntary; mandatory restrictions begin at Stage 3.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated page viewed Oct. 13, 2026; the Town's Drought Information page was last updated May 20, 2026

new_sod.summary: The Town's 2021 Drought and Water Supply Shortage Plan has no new seed or sod rules in Stages 1 and 2. In Stage 3, residents may apply for a waiver to water daily for a two-week establishment period and post Town signage in the lawn; in Stage 4, new seed and sod may be prohibited.

rebates.summary: Pays $2 per sq ft for low-water plantings or $1 per sq ft for low-water grasses, up to $2,000 per water account per year, with a 200 sq ft minimum and design approval before work; artificial turf is not eligible. 2026 funding was fully committed as of Aug. 18, 2026, and the program is expected to restart in early 2027.

For Town of Erie utility customers buying between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2026: $100 for a WaterSense smart irrigation controller, $3 per high-efficiency nozzle (up to 24), 50% of drip equipment cost (up to $75) and up to $50 per rain barrel (2 maximum).
Free sprinkler consultations from Resource Central from June through September, including a customized watering schedule.
Erie residents get a discount on Resource Central waterwise garden kits, which start at $127.

other.summary: Lot owners must keep the sidewalks next to their lot in repair (Municipal Code 7-1-4) and maintain landscaping in the right-of-way that borders their property. The right-of-way often extends past the sidewalk into what looks like the yard.

Planting, pruning, removing or treating any tree in the public right-of-way (between curb and sidewalk) requires a Tree Work Permit from the Town Forester. Street-tree planting is allowed March 15 to June 15 and Sept. 1 to Oct. 15, and adjacent property owners are responsible for maintaining street trees.
Lawn sprinkler systems and fences require a building permit.

permit_office.name: Town of Platteville (Town Hall). Contractor SAFEbuilt handles plan review and building inspections for the Town, and completed applications are submitted to Town Hall.

water_provider.name: Central Weld County Water District (supplier); billed by Town of Platteville Utility Billing
water_provider.summary: Central Weld County Water District supplies Platteville's drinking water, and the Town bills customers for metered water use.

watering_rules.summary: No lawn or landscape watering is allowed between 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. Even-numbered addresses may water Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday, odd-numbered addresses Saturday, Monday and Wednesday, and the Town says the restrictions are strictly enforced.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated standing rules (page viewed Oct. 13, 2026); the page cites Central Weld County Water District's Water Use Restrictions Plan adopted in 2015

new_sod.summary: A free SOD/Seed Watering Permit allows new lawns to be watered outside the normal days and hours. It is good for one month, with one renewal allowed.

other.summary: The Town is responsible for repairing and building sidewalks, most of which sit on private property; report deteriorating walks to Town Hall. Residents must clear snow from sidewalks within 24 hours.
A $20 temporary use permit, valid for 30 days, is required before placing a roll-off dumpster on private property.

permit_office.name: City of Greeley Building Inspection Department
permit_office.summary: Residential building permits are issued by the City's building official through Building Inspection (1100 10th Street); applications and inspection requests go through the City's eTRAKiT portal.

row_permit.summary: Greeley Code Sec. 18-2 requires a permit before building, altering or repairing any sidewalk, curb, gutter, driveway or curb cut in the public right-of-way; Public Works Permits issues these as Public Space permits through eTrakit, and the General Construction subtype covers driveways and concrete work. Applicants need a City business license and contractor's license (Code Sec. 18-3 calls for a public right-of-way contractor's license and liability insurance naming the City), and the permittee warrants the work for two years (Sec. 18-5).

flatwork_permit.summary: Greeley's amendment to the residential code's permit exemptions states that all flatwork requires a permit (Code Sec. 22-78). Code Sec. 22-99 requires nonbearing flatwork for patios, porches, stoops, walks, sidewalks and driveways to be at least 3.5 inches of concrete on undisturbed soil or compacted gravel fill.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls not over 4 ft tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, are exempt from a building permit unless they support a surcharge; taller or surcharged walls need a permit (Code Sec. 22-78, amending IRC R105.2 of the 2021 IRC).

water_provider.name: Greeley Water and Sewer (City of Greeley)

watering_rules.summary: Lawn watering is allowed April 15 to October 31 and never between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.; residential customers not on a water budget may water up to three days a week (even addresses Sun/Tue/Thu, odd addresses Mon/Wed/Sat), residential customers on a water budget may water any day, and commercial, multifamily and HOA customers water Tue/Fri/Sun. No lawn watering November 1 to April 14 without a variance; trees may be watered October through March.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Water and Sewer Board declared an adequate water year on April 15, 2026)

new_sod.summary: A free Lawn Installation Variance is required to install, replace, patch or renovate 250 sq ft or more of lawn (seed, sod or overseeding), and bluegrass-type turf needs 4 cubic yards of compost per 1,000 sq ft tilled 6 to 8 inches deep. The variance allows extra watering for 30 days with a raised water budget; the homeowner or landscape installer applies online with receipts for the seed or sod and compost plus proof of tilling.

rebates.summary: 50% of cost for a professional-grade smart controller and required accessories (up to $300), ET/rain/wind/soil sensors, pressure-reducing heads, rotary nozzles on pressure-reducing heads, pressure-reducing valves and drip zone conversion kits. The homeowner (not the contractor) applies through utility-portal.greeleyco.gov within 90 days of purchase, subject to available funds.

The City offers free water efficiency assessments for homes and recommends one before changing an irrigation system; products recommended in the assessment report are eligible for the irrigation rebates.
Listed on Greeley's Save Water page as a yard revamp with climate-adapted plants, ordered through Resource Central (resourcecentral.org); the City page does not list prices.

backflow.summary: Greeley's cross-connection program (Code Sec. 20-191) requires backflow preventers on commercial, industrial and multi-unit residential connections to be tested by an ASSE- or ABPA-certified technician at installation and annually, with records submitted within five days; single-family connections are not among the connection types the section lists. Test reports are uploaded through the City's Spry Backflow portal (Backflow program 970-336-4012).

other.summary: Adjacent property owners pay for sidewalk, curb and gutter repairs; if repairs aren't made within 60 days of notice, the City can do the work and bill the owner the cost plus 10% (Code Secs. 18-6, 18-7).
Starting January 1, 2027, general and specialty trade contractors need a City of Greeley contractor license before applying for Building Inspection permits (City notice dated August 10, 2026).
A written City permit is required before planting any plant material other than lawn in the public right-of-way (tree lawn).

permit_office.name: City of Evans Building Division
permit_office.summary: The Building Division handles plan review, building permits and inspections; applications are submitted through the City's CitizenServe portal.

row_permit.summary: Evans Engineering reviews and issues permits for all work in the public right-of-way (Code 12.04.040), and any new private driveway access to a public street needs an Access Permit from Public Works (Code 12.10.020). Residential curb cuts are limited to 24 ft with at least 10 ft between cuts (Code 12.08.050), and excavation permits must be pulled by a bonded contractor at least 48 hours before work.

flatwork_permit.summary: The City's Building FAQs list concrete flatwork as not requiring a building permit, but note that driveway expansions may require an Access Permit.

retaining_wall.summary: Evans enforces the 2018 International Residential Code (Code 15.09.010); its local amendments to the IRC permit exemptions (R105.2) change only the shed, fence (6 ft) and shingle-repair items, leaving the IRC retaining-wall exemption (walls up to 4 ft, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, that do not support a surcharge) unchanged. City handouts do not restate the threshold.

water_provider.name: City of Evans water utility (Public Works and Utilities)
water_provider.summary: The City runs the water utility. Some developments get non-potable irrigation water from the Evans Ditch system or other ditch companies, with the City supplying potable water (at potable rates) until ditch water is available.

watering_rules.summary: Under the drought emergency and Emergency Ordinance 860-26 adopted April 21, 2026, outdoor watering is allowed April 15 to October 15 only on assigned days and never 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.: even addresses Sun/Tue/Thu, odd addresses Mon/Wed/Sat, multifamily and commercial Sun/Tue/Fri.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (drought emergency declared April 21, 2026; City news release April 28, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Evans Code 13.04.200(A)(3)(b) normally lets newly seeded or sodded lawns under three months old be watered any day at any time, but the code says drought-emergency restrictions supersede that section, and the City's 2026 drought pages do not mention a new-lawn exemption. Confirm with Evans Customer Service (970-475-1170) before relying on it.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluations (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free sprinkler evaluation with a custom watering schedule; some participants may be eligible for a new smart controller. Sign up on the 2026 waitlist at resourcecentral.org/sprinklers.
$25 discounted water-wise garden kits for Evans residents; 2026 sales opened March 4 through resourcecentral.org/gardens.

backflow.summary: Evans' cross-connection rules (Code ch. 13.24) cover commercial, industrial and multi-family connections and do not apply to single-family connections unless the City finds a cross connection there. Required assemblies are tested by a certified technician at installation and at least annually, and the tester uploads results to BSI Online (bsionline.com).

other.summary: State law requires a utility locate before digging: call 811 (or UNCC at 1-800-922-1987) and allow at least 48 hours before you dig.

Tree Assistance Program: the City may reimburse up to $275 for an approved tree purchase (one per household per year); 2026 applications run April 1 to October 1, and trees bought before approval don't qualify.
Evans does not issue contractor licenses, but anyone doing business in city limits needs a City business license.

permit_office.name: Town of Garden City (building inspections by ProCode Inc.)
permit_office.summary: The Town takes building permit applications through its CommunityCore portal and contracts with ProCode Inc. for building inspections; Town Hall is (970) 351-0041.

row_permit.summary: Town Code Sec. 11-2-10 requires a permit before building, altering or repairing any sidewalk, curb, gutter, driveway or curb cut in the public right-of-way, and Sec. 11-2-30 requires Town approval for any driveway or curb cut that accesses a public street. Apply to the Town Clerk and pay the permit fee and refundable deposit set in the Town fee schedule (Secs. 11-2-90, 11-2-100).

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's permit chart lists sidewalks not more than 30 inches above grade and replacement of an existing driveway as exempt from a building permit; new driveways are not addressed (a driveway or curb cut onto a public street needs Town approval under Code Sec. 11-2-30).

retaining_wall.summary: A building permit is required for retaining walls over 4 ft tall; walls under 4 ft are exempt.

water_provider.name: City of Greeley Water and Sewer
water_provider.summary: The Town's utility page lists the City of Greeley (970-350-9811) for water and sewer service.

watering_rules.summary: Garden City is served by Greeley Water, whose 2026 rules apply to all Greeley water customers: lawn watering April 15 to October 31, no watering 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., and residential customers not on a water budget limited to three days a week (even addresses Sun/Tue/Thu, odd addresses Mon/Wed/Sat). Customers on a water budget may water any day, and commercial, multifamily and HOA customers water Tue/Fri/Sun.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Greeley declared an adequate water year on April 15, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Greeley Water requires a free Lawn Installation Variance to install, replace, patch or renovate 250 sq ft or more of lawn, with 4 cubic yards of compost per 1,000 sq ft for bluegrass-type turf; the variance allows extra watering for 30 days with a raised water budget.

rebates.program: Residential Landscape Improvement and Water Rebate Program
rebates.summary: Rebates half of a household's May to August water bills, up to $400 per the Town's application form (the code default is $300 unless the Board sets another amount), one per household; apply by the last business day in May with a before photo and planned landscape improvements, then submit photos and summer bills by September 15. Offered only in years the Board of Trustees funds it (Code Art. 5).

Reimburses up to 50% of approved exterior improvement costs, including landscaping, up to $3,000 per property per year; requires two contractor estimates and Board of Trustees approval, with work finished within five months.

backflow.summary: A Town building permit is required to install a lawn sprinkler backflow prevention device. Garden City's water comes from Greeley, whose annual backflow testing program (Greeley Code Sec. 20-191) covers commercial, industrial and multi-unit residential connections rather than single-family homes.

other.summary: Owners or occupants must keep adjoining sidewalks in good repair and clear snow from residential sidewalks within 24 hours after a storm (Code Secs. 11-1-10, 11-1-20).

Tree Care and Removal Assistance Program: the Town may pay up to 80% of proper tree care, capped at $800 per applicant, for work pre-approved by the Town Clerk and done by a tree company licensed in Greeley or Evans; apply before November 10 (Code Art. 6).

permit_office.name: Town of Kersey Building Inspection Department (inspections by SAFEbuilt Colorado)
permit_office.summary: The Town contracts with SAFEbuilt Colorado (Windsor office) for building inspection services; contractors register through the Town's CommunityCore portal.

row_permit.summary: A Town permit, approved by the Town Manager or Board of Trustees, is required to repair, replace or modify any sidewalk in the public right-of-way (Code Sec. 11-17). The Land Development Code limits a single-family lot to one driveway curb cut no wider than 20 ft onto a local or collector street (Sec. 20-8).

flatwork_permit.summary: Kersey's published rules don't say whether private flatwork needs a building permit; its IRC amendment requires exterior concrete flatwork (porches, patios, sidewalks, driveways and steps) at new dwellings, including warranty repair or replacement work, to be reinforced with at least 10-gauge welded wire mesh or other approved reinforcement (Code Sec. 18-45).

retaining_wall.summary: Kersey enforces the 2024 IRC (Code Sec. 18-44, Ord. 2025-0010); its amendments to the IRC permit exemptions (R105.2) change only the shed, fence (6 ft) and shingle-repair items, leaving the IRC retaining-wall exemption (walls up to 4 ft, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, that do not support a surcharge) unchanged.

water_provider.name: Town of Kersey (water purchased from Central Weld County Water District)
water_provider.summary: The Town buys water from Central Weld County Water District and distributes it through a gravity system; the Kersey Mobile Home Park is subject to Central Weld's regulations rather than the Town's water-use rules (Code Sec. 13-343).

watering_rules.summary: From March 1 through October 31, watering landscaped areas, gardens, trees and shrubs with hose-end sprinklers or automatic systems is prohibited from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily, with no restrictions November 1 through February. Minimum fines are $100 for a first offense and $200 for a second, and the Board may impose further limits by resolution.
watering_rules.as_of: Standing rule in Kersey Municipal Code Sec. 13-342 (code updated September 9, 2026); no separate 2026 notice found

new_sod.summary: The Town Clerk may issue a permit exempting newly seeded or sodded lawns from the watering rules for up to two months, allowing watering every day at any time; the permit must be displayed in a door window or the window closest to the door (Code Sec. 13-346).

backflow.summary: Kersey's cross-connection rules (Code Sec. 13-320) require backflow assemblies on commercial, industrial and multi-family connections to be tested by a certified technician at installation and annually; single-family connections are exempt unless a cross connection is found. Test results go to Kersey Public Works by email or mail.

other.summary: Property owners must repair or replace unsafe sidewalks next to their property, while the Town repairs curb and gutter and rollover curb-sidewalks (Code Secs. 11-17, 11-18).
Fences need a Town permit, with a drawing showing property lines and setbacks.

permit_office.name: Town of LaSalle (inspections by ProCode Inc.)
permit_office.summary: Town Hall front-office staff process building permit applications (now through CommunityCore), and the Town contracts with ProCode Inc. (970-305-3161) for inspections.

row_permit.summary: Building a sidewalk, curb or gutter requires a permit from the Town Clerk, with a fee and staking by the Town's engineer (Code Sec. 11-45); cutting any street or alley surface requires Town Clerk permission and a fee, and the cut must be patched within 10 days (Secs. 11-71, 11-72).

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's Building Permits page lists patios, sprinkler systems and fences among projects that require a building permit; driveways and other flatwork are not addressed.

retaining_wall.summary: LaSalle enforces the 2024 IRC (Code Sec. 18-143, Ord. 19-2025); its amendments to the IRC permit exemptions (R105.2) change only the shed and shingle-repair items, leaving the IRC retaining-wall exemption (walls up to 4 ft, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, that do not support a surcharge) unchanged.

water_provider.name: Town of LaSalle
water_provider.summary: The Town owns the water, which Central Weld County Water District treats; the Dove Hill subdivision also has a Town non-potable water system.

watering_rules.summary: Town water customers (except Dove Hill): odd addresses water Saturday, Monday and Wednesday, even addresses Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday, no watering on Fridays, and no watering 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Dove Hill's non-potable system: odd addresses on odd days and even addresses on even days of the month, 15 to 20 minutes per zone.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated Town web page (checked October 2026)

new_sod.summary: The Town's watering page lists no new-sod exemption; under Phase II drought restrictions, the Director of Public Works may issue permits for extended watering of new lawns (Code Sec. 13-40).

backflow.summary: LaSalle's Backflow Prevention Cross-Connection Control Program covers non-single-family connections (commercial, industrial, multi-family, agricultural and irrigation-system connections); single-family connections that pose no potential risk are exempt. Required RPZ assemblies must be tested and certified annually, with certificates uploaded to CommunityCore and emailed to backflow@safebuilt.com.

other.summary: Owners of property next to a street or sidewalk must maintain the trees and shrubs in the abutting right-of-way (Code Sec. 11-112).
If the Town orders an unsafe sidewalk repaired and the owner doesn't fix it within three days of notice, the Town can repair it and assess the adjacent owner (Code Sec. 11-53).
The Town charges a 2% use tax on materials, and permit fees may be doubled if work starts before the permit is issued.

permit_office.name: Town of Gilcrest (building inspections by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.summary: Building permit applications are on the Town's Forms page (Town Hall 970-737-2426); the Town's posted plumbing review guidelines (rev. October 28, 2020) name SAFEbuilt as its private building inspection partner.

row_permit.summary: A Town permit is required to build or alter any sidewalk, curb, gutter, driveway or street opening, or to do any work in public property, easements or right-of-way (Code Sec. 11-21). The Excavation Permit requires a $10 application fee, a $2,000 cash deposit or surety bond, liability insurance ($200,000 per person and $1,000,000 per occurrence) and workers' comp, 48-hour notice to adjacent owners, and sign-off by the Town Engineer, Public Works and Town Administrator.

retaining_wall.summary: Gilcrest enforces the 2018 IRC (Code Sec. 18-21, Ord. 2023-03); its amendments to the IRC permit exemptions (R105.2) change only the shed and shingle-repair items, leaving the IRC retaining-wall exemption (walls up to 4 ft, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, that do not support a surcharge) unchanged.

water_provider.name: Town of Gilcrest (Public Works)
water_provider.summary: The Town provides water, sewer, trash, street lighting and stormwater service.

backflow.summary: Gilcrest's cross-connection program (Code Art. VIII) applies to commercial, industrial and multi-family connections, not single-family connections; devices are tested by a certified technician at installation and at least annually, and the tester sends reports to the Town by mail, fax or email.

other.summary: Owners or occupants must keep adjoining sidewalks in good repair and clear snow from residential sidewalks within 24 hours (Code Secs. 11-1, 11-2).
The Town's building inspection fee handout lists a $60 single-stop fee for a lawn sprinkler system.
No outdoor watering schedule is posted on the Town site; the Board of Trustees sets water conservation orders by resolution (Code Sec. 13-153), so check with Town Hall (970-737-2426).

permit_office.name: Town of Milliken Building Services (Community Development); building department functions by SAFEbuilt
permit_office.summary: Permits are submitted through CommunityCore; SAFEbuilt provides plan review, inspections and building official services, and contractors must hold a Town contractor license before a permit is issued.

row_permit.summary: A Right-of-Way permit is required for any work in Town right-of-way or easements: a Utility Excavation, Street Cut, ROW Work Permit for underground work and street cuts, and a Counter Residential Street Obstruction Permit for using streets or sidewalks during a project. Apply through CommunityCore (register as a contractor or homeowner); fees are assessed at review, and a bond may be required for excavations (Code Sec. 11-2-10).

retaining_wall.summary: Milliken enforces the 2024 IRC (Code Sec. 18-10-10, Ord. 834); its amendments to the IRC permit exemptions (R105.2) change only the shed, fence (6 ft) and shingle-repair items, leaving the IRC retaining-wall exemption (walls up to 4 ft, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, that do not support a surcharge) unchanged.

water_provider.name: Town of Milliken Water/Wastewater Department
water_provider.summary: Town water is treated by Central Weld County Water District (connecting on the south side) and the City of Greeley (from the north), and the page names a Town-owned Alluvial Well Blending Facility as the newest supply; the Town also runs non-potable irrigation from its Hillsborough Ditch shares.

watering_rules.summary: Even addresses may sprinkle Monday, Wednesday and Friday and odd addresses Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, only before 9 a.m. or after 7 p.m.; no lawn sprinkling with Town-treated water from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. or on Sundays, and no automatic irrigation November 1 to March 1. Hand watering and drip irrigation are allowed any day.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated Town page; matches Municipal Code Sec. 13-2-60 (code updated July 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: For new seed or sod, request a free watering permit from Town Hall (970-587-4331); it allows additional watering times without penalty, and you pay only for the water used.

backflow.summary: All new connections to the Town water system must have an approved backflow device, and every required assembly must be tested annually by a certified technician during its assigned test month, with results sent to the Town's backflow tracking agency within three days and failed tests reported to the Town within 24 hours (Code Sec. 13-3-30).

other.summary: A Town contractor license (Municipal Code ch. 6, art. IV) is required before the Town issues a permit, and lawn sprinkler work is listed as a counter permit.
Owners or occupants must keep adjoining sidewalks in good repair and clear snow from residential sidewalks within 24 hours (Code Secs. 11-1-10, 11-1-20).

permit_office.name: Town of Johnstown Building Department (plan review and inspections by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.summary: Permits and contractor licenses are applied for through the Town's eTRAKiT portal; SAFEbuilt provides plan review, inspections and the Chief Building Official, and all contractors must be licensed with the Town.

row_permit.summary: Any work on streets, curbs and gutters or sidewalks needs a Town Right-of-Way permit (Municipal Code Sec. 11-22), applied for through eTRAKiT at least 10 business days ahead with a site plan, an MUTCD traffic control plan and a certificate of insurance naming the Town. Work on a state highway also needs a CDOT permit, a closeout inspection must be requested 48 hours ahead, and permit extensions cost $75.

flatwork_permit.summary: No building permit is needed to pour a new concrete patio, driveway or on-site walk if it stays at least 3 ft from property lines for drainage; residential landscaping and sprinkler systems also don't need building permits.

retaining_wall.summary: The Town lists retaining walls more than 4 ft tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, as requiring a building permit, with the IRC qualifier for walls that support a surcharge or impound Class I, II or IIIA liquids.

water_provider.name: Town of Johnstown Utilities Department (Water & Sewer)
water_provider.summary: The Town runs its own water plant and distribution system. Town water rebates are limited to Town water customers and the Town says customers of other water providers are not eligible, so confirm who bills the property for water.

watering_rules.summary: The 2026 schedule (Water Conservation Level 3, Moderate) runs April 20 to October 15: addresses ending in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 (and HOA common areas and metro districts) water Monday and Thursday, addresses ending in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9 water Tuesday and Friday, and no watering 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. After October 15, only hand watering of trees and shrubs on Saturdays and Sundays when it is above 40 degrees.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (2026 Johnstown Watering Schedule, Level 3)

new_sod.summary: The Town's 2026 watering FAQ says there are currently no exemptions from the watering schedule, so new sod or seed gets no extra watering days.

rebates.summary: Pays $1 to $2 per sq ft (up to $2,000 per water account per year) as a utility credit for replacing at least 200 sq ft of turf with low- or no-water plantings or low-water grass (artificial turf not eligible), with design pre-approval, 50% living plant coverage and a final Town site visit. New 2026 applications closed June 15; the Town invites applications again next summer.

Fixed-amount utility-bill credits for qualifying outdoor irrigation products, first-come first-served; the Town's page describes its 2026 water-saving programs in the past tense and looks ahead to a 2027 program year.
Free sprinkler efficiency consultations for homeowners, two days a week from May 1 to September 1 (not for repairs such as leaks, start-ups or line breaks).

backflow.summary: Backflow devices are required on industrial, commercial, irrigation, multi-family and fire line services, including multi-family and commercial properties with irrigation systems. Every device must be tested annually by a certified tester on the same due date each year, with reports filed at BSI Online (bsionline.com) for a $16.95 fee per report.

other.summary: Call 811 (or 800-922-1987) at least three days before digging to have underground utilities located.
The Town collects a 3.5% use tax on construction materials when a building permit is issued.

permit_office.name: Town of Windsor Community Development - Building Permits (building inspections by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.summary: Residential permits are applied for through the Town's Community Core portal and issued by the Town permit desk at 200 N. 11th St.; building inspections are requested through SAFEbuilt, while Town utility, curb and gutter inspections are requested from the Town.

row_permit.summary: Work in Town rights-of-way requires an Engineering right-of-way permit from Windsor Engineering and Public Works, and the Town is moving all right-of-way applications to a new OpenGov permit portal. Utility cuts, backfill and pavement patching must meet the Town's Street Specifications.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's building permit requirements include a Soil Compaction Affidavit for concrete flatwork under Windsor Municipal Code Sec. 18-3-10 (27.8). The page does not say whether a stand-alone patio or driveway needs its own building permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Windsor (Windsor Water Utility); North Weld County Water District, City of Greeley and Fort Collins-Loveland Water District also named as providers
water_provider.summary: The Town's Water/Sewer page states that three separate water providers serve the Town of Windsor: North Weld County Water District, the City of Greeley and Fort Collins-Loveland Water District; NWCWD's service-area page says it serves the northern areas of Windsor. Some subdivisions have HOA non-potable irrigation systems, and residents contact their HOA about those.

watering_rules.summary: The Town's Efficiency page lists 'lawn watering restrictions (no watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily)' among its water-conservation measures; no day-of-week schedule or drought stage is posted on that page.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated page (checked 2026-10-13)

rebates.program: Lawn Replacement Program (Windsor ColoradoScape Initiative pilot)
rebates.summary: Pays $1-$2 per sq ft of living turf removed from a front yard (minimum 200 sq ft; maximum $2,000 per water account per year) for properties with a Town of Windsor water account (dual-use accounts excluded); designs must be approved before work starts and artificial turf is not eligible. 2026 applications ran Feb. 2-June 30, with projects completed and inspected by Oct. 16, 2026.
Windsor Utility customers get a $25 discount on Resource Central's pre-planned water-wise garden kits while limited supplies last; the program typically runs March through May.

backflow.summary: Business and industrial Windsor Water customers, including sprinkler supply lines, must have backflow assemblies tested once a year by a certified tester (Backflow Solutions Inc. sends the notices) and retested after any repair or relocation. Testing of residential sprinkler backflow devices is voluntary.

other.summary: A building permit is required to install a sprinkler system, whether it connects to Town potable water or a subdivision non-potable system.

Under setback table 16-1-20(a), patios no more than 12 in. above grade may sit in any setback if at least 3 ft from the property line, and walls or retaining walls under 4 ft (top of wall to bottom of footer) may sit in any setback subject to fence and wall standards.

permit_office.name: Town of Severance Building Department (inspections by SAFEbuilt Colorado)
permit_office.summary: The Town accepts building permit applications online only through Community Core, and all inspections for the Town are done by SAFEbuilt Colorado.

row_permit.summary: The Town's street permits page lists a Right-of-Way (ROW) Permit; completed ROW permit applications are emailed to rowpermits@townofseverance.org, with questions to the Administration Department at 970-686-1218. The page does not list specific work types or fees.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's 'What Needs a Permit' list exempts platforms, walks and driveways not more than 30 in. above ground and not over a basement or story below. The exemption does not apply to platforms, decks or landings attached to or placed next to a building.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 4 ft high need a building permit; walls 4 ft or less, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, are exempt unless they support a surcharge or impound flammable liquids.

water_provider.name: Town of Severance (Town water system); North Weld County Water District serves some subdivisions
water_provider.summary: The Town supplies water to Town water customers, while North Weld County Water District serves Belmont Farms, Bridal Hill/Saddler Ridge, Casa Loma, Golden Eagle Acres, Hidden Valley Farm and Soaring Eagle Ranch. Hunters Crossing, The Overlook, Severance Shores and Tailholt have approved non-potable irrigation systems.

watering_rules.summary: For Town water customers, even-numbered addresses (last two digits) water Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday and odd-numbered addresses Monday, Wednesday and Saturday (HOA common areas, multifamily and non-residential properties Sunday, Wednesday and Friday), with no watering 11 a.m.-5 p.m. and no lawn watering Dec. 1-Mar. 31. Hand watering of flowers, shrubs and trees is allowed daily during permitted hours with a shut-off nozzle; the rules do not apply to approved non-potable systems or NWCWD-served subdivisions.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated page; standing rules under Resolution No. 2013-07R

new_sod.summary: The Town Administrator may grant a variance from the watering restrictions to establish new lawns or landscaping (variance permits are issued for newly seeded or sodded lawns); variance permits expire no more than 30 days after issuance.

backflow.summary: The Town's permit list requires a building permit, with a backflow preventer inspection, for lawn sprinkler systems connected to the water supply if a backflow preventer was not installed during the original build.
backflow.note: No annual residential backflow-test requirement was found on the Town site.

other.summary: The Town's watering guidelines state that building permits are required for the installation of all sprinkler systems.
Contractors performing work within the Town must hold a Town of Severance contractor license.
In NWCWD-served subdivisions, North Weld County Water District's May 2026 newsletter asks customers to voluntarily water no more than three days a week and only before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m.

permit_office.name: Town of Eaton Building and Permitting (inspections contracted to SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.summary: Permits are applied for and issued through the Town's CommunityCore portal, and the Town contracts with SAFEbuilt for all building inspection services; the 2024 I-codes took effect Jan. 1, 2026 (Ordinance 664).

row_permit.summary: Work in Town right-of-way needs a Right-of-Way Use Permit (form effective Jan. 1, 2026) submitted to Eaton Public Works & Engineering; the standard application and review fee is $175, a traffic control plan must be included, and restoration is due within 10 days of project completion.

water_provider.name: Town of Eaton water utility (treated water purchased from North Weld County Water District)
water_provider.summary: Eaton's 2025 Drinking Water Quality Report lists the Town's source as surface water purchased from North Weld County Water District (consecutive connection). The Town also serves non-potable irrigation customers, whose systems run April 15-Oct. 15.

watering_rules.summary: Potable and non-potable residential customers: even-numbered addresses water Monday, Wednesday and Friday and odd-numbered addresses Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, with no watering 10 a.m.-6 p.m. HOA common areas water every other day, and non-potable systems run April 15-Oct. 15 (Resolutions 2019-07 and 2019-08).
watering_rules.as_of: Undated page; Resolutions 2019-07 (potable) and 2019-08 (non-potable)

new_sod.summary: Residents establishing new lawns or landscaping can get a yellow permit from Town Hall (970-454-3338) that allows daily watering for 30 days; the permit must be displayed where it is visible from the street.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluations (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free sprinkler efficiency evaluations with a custom watering schedule and recommendations, offered to Eaton residents June through September through the Town's Resource Central partnership.

Low-water garden kits with pollinator-friendly starter plants and a plant-by-number map, offered through the Town's Resource Central partnership; residents can join an interest list to be notified when kits go on sale.

backflow.summary: The Town's backflow program covers non-single-family connections (commercial, industrial, multifamily, agricultural, irrigation) and single-family connections that pose a potential risk, listing irrigation lines among greater-risk connections. Required RPZ assemblies must be tested and certified annually, with certifications uploaded to the Town's CommunityCore tracking system.

other.summary: Lawn sprinkler and backflow work is permitted on the Town's over-the-counter building permit application.

permit_office.name: Town of Ault (Town Hall licensing; inspections by SAFEbuilt Colorado)
permit_office.summary: The Town accepts building permit applications online only through CommunityCore; exterior projects or projects that change a foundation need a letter to the Planning Commission, and applicants contact SAFEbuilt for all required inspections.

row_permit.summary: A Town of Ault ROW permit application and diagram must be returned to Town Hall before any work in the right-of-way. The ROW/street cut permit is $150 plus street/ROW repair, boring is $100 per bore, inspections are $100 scheduled or $150 unscheduled, and ROW violations are $500 per incident.

water_provider.name: Town of Ault Municipal Utilities (Colorado-Big Thompson water treated at Soldier Canyon, delivered by North Weld County Water District)
water_provider.summary: The Town's potable water comes from the Colorado-Big Thompson project, is filtered at the Soldier Canyon filter plant and is delivered by North Weld County Water District. Non-potable (untreated well water) irrigation serves certain areas of town, including the Conestoga neighborhood, and operates April 15-Oct. 15.

watering_rules.summary: Potable customers (2024 schedule): even-numbered houses water Sunday, Tuesday and Friday and odd-numbered houses Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, with no watering 10 a.m.-5 p.m.; the potable schedule is set yearly. Non-potable customers (including Conestoga) water on even or odd calendar days matching their house number, with no watering 10 a.m.-6 p.m., per Ault Municipal Code 13.04.400(2)(A)-(B).
watering_rules.as_of: Spring-fall 2024 notice (latest posted; no 2025 or 2026 potable schedule found)

other.summary: Projects within the Conestoga metro district need a project approval letter from the district before a Town building permit application is submitted.

permit_office.name: Town of Pierce (permitting run for the Town by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.summary: The Town issues building permits (applications through CommunityCore), with permitting run for the Town by SAFEbuilt; inspections are booked with SAFEbuilt at 970-674-1036.

row_permit.summary: Under Resolution 2026-05 (adopted April 13, 2026), any excavation, construction, installation or other work in the Town's public right-of-way needs a right-of-way permit from the Town Clerk, filed at least 24 hours before work, with a $175 standard fee, a performance or cash bond, and liability insurance naming the Town. Permittees must call 811, give Public Works two business days' notice, and restore any disturbed sidewalks, curbs, gutters and landscaping.

water_provider.name: Town of Pierce water system (treated water supplied by North Weld County Water District)
water_provider.summary: North Weld County Water District supplies the Town with treated water (Colorado-Big Thompson water filtered at the Soldier Canyon plant), which the Town distributes through about 7 miles of mains with a meter at each tap.

watering_rules.summary: Even-numbered addresses water on even-numbered days and odd-numbered addresses on odd-numbered days, with no watering between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.
watering_rules.as_of: Posted April 14, 2026
