permit_office.name: Town of Nunn Town Clerk's office (plan review and all inspections by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.summary: Building permits are applied for at the Town Clerk's office, which forwards plans to SAFEbuilt; buildings over 120 sq ft also need Planning Board approval, and all inspections are requested from SAFEbuilt.

row_permit.summary: Nunn Municipal Code Ch. 12.12 requires a right-of-way construction permit from the Town Clerk, in consultation with the Town Engineer, for any construction or excavation in a public street or right-of-way, including installing curb, gutter, sidewalk or a driveway. Curb, gutter and sidewalk permits require an irrevocable letter of credit for 115% of the estimated cost, and fees follow the Town fee schedule.

retaining_wall.summary: The Town's list of projects that typically require a building permit includes retaining walls over 4 ft in height.

water_provider.name: Town of Nunn water utility (treated surface water purchased from North Weld County Water District)
water_provider.summary: The Town of Nunn provides water service, and its 2026 Water Quality Report lists the source as surface water purchased from North Weld County Water District.

watering_rules.summary: Municipal Code Sec. 13.12.020 lets the Town Board set a lawn-and-garden watering schedule by resolution for high-use months, with violation penalties added to the property's water bill.
watering_rules.as_of: 2024 Municipal Code; no current schedule posted on the Town website

other.summary: Lawn sprinkler system connections to the water supply are on the Town's list of projects that typically require a building permit.

The Town owns and maintains the water line from the main to the curb box; the property owner owns and maintains the service line from the curb box to the home, and service-line work must be done by a licensed plumber (Code Sec. 13.08.070).

permit_office.name: Town of Mead Building Division (inspections contracted to SAFEbuilt Colorado)
permit_office.summary: The Building Division reviews applications, issues permits and enforces building codes, and the Town contracts with SAFEbuilt Colorado for building inspections.

row_permit.summary: Anyone wanting a driveway or curb cut onto a Town road must contact the Town; new driveways need a Street, Driveway & Culvert Permit ($250 for a driveway or culvert, generally one access per parcel, with liability insurance and a two-year warranty on right-of-way work). Any excavation or work in a street, alley, sidewalk or public place needs a Utility Excavation, Street Cut & Obstruction Permit ($50 base fee plus road-cut, inspection and use-tax charges), and the Town Engineer oversees right-of-way permitting.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's 'Do I Need a Building Permit?' page lists flatwork (patios, sidewalks and driveways) under 'Permit Not Required', but advises checking with the Building Division about specific code requirements.

water_provider.name: Little Thompson Water District and Longs Peak Water District
water_provider.summary: The Town's Water Service page says water service in Mead is provided by Little Thompson Water District (ltwd.org) and Longs Peak Water District (lpwd.org); it does not say which areas each district serves.

watering_rules.summary: Little Thompson Water District customers are under a Water Shortage Watch as of April 2026: water only before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m., at most three days a week (even addresses Monday, Wednesday, Saturday; odd addresses Tuesday, Thursday, Sunday), with trees and shrubs on drip, hand watering, deep-root needle or arbor bag. Violations draw a written warning, then fines of $100, $200 and $300.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (LTWD Water Shortage Watch as of April 2026)
watering_rules.note: Applies to LTWD customers; no watering schedule was found on the Longs Peak Water District website.

new_sod.summary: Under LTWD's drought matrix, the new-lawn permit provision is not applicable at the Watch level in effect as of April 2026; at Levels I and II, new lawns from seed or sod need an LTWD permit (June 1-Sept. 15) that allows watering any time and day as defined in the permit, and at Level III new lawns are not allowed.

rebates.program: Lawn Replacement Program (LTWD with Resource Central)
rebates.summary: LTWD customers removing at least 200 sq ft of healthy turf can get up to $750 off Resource Central's lawn removal ($1 instead of $2.75 per sq ft, up to 454 sq ft) or toward up to four Garden In A Box kits for DIY projects. The 2026 program is closed; a 2027 interest list is open.
Up to $500 back for adding at least 3 cubic yards of compost or other amendment per 1,000 sq ft, loosening the top 8 in. of soil and mixing the amendment into the top 4-6 in.
Up to $300 back on eligible xeric or drought-resistant plants and trees, submitted with an itemized receipt.
Up to $125 back for a WaterSense-labeled irrigation controller.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluations (LTWD with Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free 75-minute sprinkler evaluations for LTWD customers; the 2026 season is closed and a 2027 interest list is open.

rebates.program: Garden In A Box (LTWD with Resource Central)
rebates.summary: $25 discount for LTWD customers on water-wise garden kits; 2026 discounts are sold out.

backflow.summary: LTWD requires backflow assemblies on sprinkler and irrigation systems; non-residential customers, HOAs and residential customers with high-hazard connections must have devices tested annually by a certified tester and submit reports to LTWD. Standard home sprinkler systems are not considered high hazard, so residential test reporting is not required, though LTWD recommends a pressure vacuum breaker tested annually.

other.summary: Installing a lawn sprinkler system requires a building permit (a one-stop permit), but adding zones to an existing sprinkler system does not.

permit_office.name: City of Fort Collins Building Services
permit_office.summary: Building Services reviews plans, issues building permits, performs inspections and licenses contractors; permit submittals go to buildingservices@fortcollins.gov (970-416-2740).

row_permit.summary: The Engineering Department requires a Sidewalk and Drive Approach Permit for any work on sidewalks or driveway approaches ($25 for up to 15 ft plus $0.30 per additional foot) and an Excavation Permit whenever cutting is done in City right-of-way. Contractors must hold a City-issued Right-of-Way Contractor's License for their work category.

flatwork_permit.summary: The City lists 'Sidewalks and Driveways' among residential work that does not need a building permit; a patio or porch cover does need one.

retaining_wall.summary: Residential retaining walls up to 4 ft, measured from the low-side grade to the top, are exempt unless supporting a surcharge, and a second wall uphill must be set back at least the full height of the lower wall. Taller walls need a permit and must be designed and stamped by a Colorado-licensed structural engineer.

water_provider.name: Fort Collins Utilities
water_provider.summary: Fort Collins Utilities serves much of the city, but some addresses are served by other water providers (the City links a provider map and tells those customers to check with their own provider). The Fort Collins-Loveland Water District, for example, serves parts of Fort Collins, Loveland, Timnath and Windsor.

watering_rules.summary: A voluntary Water Shortage Watch has applied to Fort Collins Utilities customers since May 1, 2026: water lawns no more than two days a week (no more than 1 inch per week) and not between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.; hand, drip and deep-root watering of trees and gardens is allowed any time. Utilities also suggests a voluntary turf schedule of Mon/Wed/Sat for odd addresses and Tue/Thu/Sun for even addresses.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Watch effective May 1, 2026; still listed as the current level)

new_sod.summary: Fort Collins Utilities lists new seed and sod establishment as grounds for an exception permit to assigned watering days, with applications available when a water shortage (mandatory restrictions) is declared; the current Watch is voluntary. Utilities also asks that new sod not be overwatered so water does not run onto sidewalks or into storm drains.

rebates.summary: Pays $0.75 per sq ft, up to $750 (1,000 sq ft), plus a native-plant bonus, to replace grass with an approved low-water landscape; projects must be approved before installation. The residential application is closed for the rest of 2026, with updates expected in January 2027.

Bill-credit rebates at Fort Collins Utilities residential addresses, for example up to $65 for a weather-based controller, up to $4 per rotary nozzle, up to $130 per drip zone and up to $260 for a pressure reducing valve (pre-approval required). Apply within 60 days of purchase.
Free professional sprinkler evaluation through Resource Central for homes and rental properties, including a custom watering schedule; a DIY evaluation kit can also be borrowed.
Discounted spring and late-summer water-wise garden kits for Utilities water customers; limited and first come, first served.

backflow.summary: All sprinkler systems must have an approved backflow preventer, and City guidance says to have a certified tester inspect it at least every three years (questions: cross-connection@fortcollins.gov). Building Services issues a fast-track Lawn Sprinkler and Backflow Preventer permit ($65 building permit fee) that closes only after a third-party test by a certified backflow tester.

other.summary: The City's Water Shortage Watch and restrictions apply only to Fort Collins Utilities water customers; customers of other providers should follow their own provider's rules, and properties irrigating with well or raw water are exempt.

permit_office.name: City of Loveland Building Division (Development Services)
permit_office.summary: A building permit is required for new construction, additions or alterations; residential applications are emailed to eplan-res@cityofloveland.org. City pages also refer to the division as the Building Department.

row_permit.summary: A Minor Right-of-Way permit is required for concrete work such as driveway approaches and sidewalks, and a Major ROW permit for any other work in the right-of-way; applications go to Public Works (2525 W. 1st St. or engineering@cityofloveland.org) with a certificate of insurance and a traffic control plan. Working without a ROW permit costs double fees or $500, whichever is more.

water_provider.name: Loveland Water and Power (City of Loveland Utilities)
water_provider.summary: Loveland Water and Power serves more than 25,000 homes and businesses in a 33-square-mile territory. The Fort Collins-Loveland Water District also serves parts of Loveland.

watering_rules.summary: No mandatory 2026 watering schedule is posted. Loveland Water and Power's June 1, 2026 summer guide recommends watering about three times a week during cooler hours, avoiding midday heat, windy days and watering right after rain, and checking its Water page or calling 970-962-3355 for current rules.

rebates.summary: Loveland Water and Power says residential water rebates, including those for weather-based irrigation controllers and efficient irrigation equipment, are currently unavailable, with details on the 2026 application process to follow.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluations, Garden In A Box and Resource Central seminars
rebates.summary: Listed by Loveland Water and Power as residential water-saving programs: sprinkler system evaluations from Slow the Flow, Garden In A Box home gardens and Waterwise seminars from Resource Central.

backflow.summary: Dedicated irrigation backflow assemblies must be tested at least annually by a certified cross-connection control technician, and single-family homeowners are encouraged to test annually. Testers send reports to Loveland Water and Power (200 N. Wilson Ave.; questions 970-962-3721).

other.summary: A free sprinkler permit is required to install a new sprinkler system or to repair, expand or modify an existing system with an approved backflow assembly; normal maintenance such as replacing heads or repairing a leak does not need one.

permit_office.name: Town of Berthoud Building Department (Community Development)
permit_office.summary: Handles building permits and inspections through the CommunityCore portal under the 2024 I-Codes; SAFEbuilt performs building inspections for the Town, and contractors must be licensed with the Town before applying.

row_permit.summary: A Town Right-of-Way Permit (Engineering Department) is required before any work or obstruction in the public right-of-way. Apply through CommunityCore with a certificate of insurance naming the Town, workers' compensation coverage and, when traffic or walkways are affected, a traffic control plan.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's partial list of projects requiring a building permit names decks, patio covers and enclosures, larger sheds and pergolas, pools and re-roofs, but does not list driveways, sidewalks or on-grade patios; it notes the list may not be all-inclusive and to contact the Building Department.

retaining_wall.summary: The Town's Engineering and Infrastructure Design Standards (effective Jan. 10, 2026) require retaining walls 4 ft or taller to be designed, stamped and signed by a registered professional engineer and approved and permitted through the Town.

water_provider.name: Town of Berthoud Water & Wastewater Utilities
water_provider.summary: Operates the Town's drinking water system for residents, businesses and surrounding service areas. The Town owns the main and connection up to the curb stop; the service line from the curb stop to the house is the owner's responsibility.

watering_rules.summary: Berthoud currently has no mandatory water restrictions, but residents are asked to follow voluntary restrictions and use water sparingly; Town code requires lawn irrigation to be done between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m. Restrictions, when in effect, are posted on the Water Utilities page and Town homepage.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated Town page; current when checked 2026-10-13

new_sod.summary: Ordinance 967 bans irrigation from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. but allows hand watering, soaker hoses, drip irrigation and irrigation of newly laid sod and newly seeded lawns at any time.

rebates.program: Resource Central sprinkler evaluations, Garden In A Box and Waterwise Yard Seminars
rebates.summary: Listed as water-saving resources on the Town's Drought Water Usage page; the page lists no rebate or turf-replacement program run by the Town.

backflow.summary: Berthoud's Non-Residential Cross-Connection Control Program (Code 6.28) requires backflow assemblies to be tested at installation and at least once a year by a certified technician approved by CDPHE and the Town, with records kept by the customer and the Town Water Department. The annual test rule does not apply to residential dual-check installations.

other.summary: Property owners are responsible for repairing sidewalks next to their property (Municipal Code Ch. 15.11). Under the Sidewalk Cost-Share Program, the Town inspects a reported failed sidewalk, the owner gets at least three contractor bids for Town approval, and the Town reimburses after inspection and proof of payment.

Abutting property owners maintain trees in the right-of-way, and removing or replacing a street tree involves a Street Tree Work Permit. The Street Tree Replacement Cost Share reimburses 50% of a replacement tree or planting, up to $400 per frontage per year.
Call 811 or 800-922-1987 at least three days before any digging; the Town notes this is required by law.

permit_office.name: Town of Timnath Building Services (Community Development Department)
permit_office.summary: Building Services processes all building permit applications; plan revisions are sent to SAFEbuilt Colorado Plan Review.

row_permit.summary: Street cuts, street occupancy and curb cuts in the public right-of-way need a Town Right-of-Way Permit approved by the Town Engineer ($50 application for concrete-only work; $100 per curb cut), with 5 working days' notice before starting. The Driveway Approach Policy requires a ROW permit and a Town-licensed contractor to remove curb and gutter for a driveway approach, and prohibits removing mountable curb where the sidewalk is attached.

water_provider.name: Varies by subdivision: Fort Collins-Loveland Water District (FCLWD), East Larimer County Water District (ELCO) or North Weld County Water District
water_provider.summary: Per the Town's district list, FCLWD serves Old Town, Harmony, Timnath Ranch, Timnath South, Timnath Landing, Summerfields Estates, Rendezvous and Fairview Village; ELCO serves Fisher Farm and Serratoga Falls; North Weld County Water District serves Wildwing.

watering_rules.summary: Rules depend on the water district. ELCO's 2026 voluntary restrictions ask customers to water lawns no more than 2 days per week (after the last frost, typically mid-May) and to avoid watering between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.; FCLWD says conservation is encouraged but remains voluntary and sets no watering days or hours.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (ELCO May 2026 notice)

rebates.summary: Bill credits of $100 for an EPA WaterSense-certified smart controller, $25 for a rain sensor and up to $4 per rotary sprinkler nozzle; all FCLWD customers are eligible.

rebates.program: FCLWD Garden In A Box credit
rebates.summary: $25 bill credit for FCLWD customers who buy a Resource Central Garden In A Box.
Free Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluations through Resource Central for ELCO residential and non-residential customers; register with the water account number.

backflow.summary: FCLWD requires backflow assemblies to be tested annually by a certified tester with reports sent to the District, and recommends single-family irrigation systems be tested every three years. ELCO requires annual testing for non-single-family services, including irrigation, with results reported through the BSI online portal; single-family homes are generally outside its program.

other.summary: The adjacent property owner maintains the Town-owned tree lawn. Replacement landscaping must reach at least 75% live plant cover at maturity with plants no taller than 24 inches, changes from the approved plan need Town review, and rubber mulch, plastic weed barrier, poured concrete and fences are not allowed.

permit_office.name: Town of Wellington Building Department (Building & Planning)
permit_office.summary: Permits are applied for online through Community Core; SAFEbuilt, the Building Department's partner, conducts plan review, issues permits and schedules inspections. All contractors and subcontractors need a Town contractor license before applying.

row_permit.summary: A Right of Way Permit (street cut permit) from Public Works is required any time work or cutting is done in the Town right-of-way, including sidewalk work. It requires a liability insurance certificate, traffic control plan and current contractor/business license, costs $100 plus a $1,000 refundable deposit, and takes about 72 hours to review.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's 'Do I Need a Permit?' guide lists flatwork as needing a permit only when it is part of the egress system, such as steps, landings and ramps.

retaining_wall.summary: A permit is required for retaining walls 4 ft or higher, measured from the bottom of the footings; it is a one-stop permit with no plan review.

water_provider.name: Town of Wellington Municipal Utilities
water_provider.summary: The Town's Municipal Utilities provides metered water, wastewater and stormwater service.

watering_rules.summary: Voluntary Irrigation and Water Conservation Guidelines (Resolution 15-2025) are in effect April 15 to October 15, 2026: water outdoors only between 7 p.m. and 8 a.m. and water turf no more than two days a week. Suggested days are Tuesday and Saturday for odd street numbers and Wednesday and Sunday for even street numbers.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (April 15 to October 15, 2026)

new_sod.summary: The guidelines allow extra watering for new grass seed, sod and landscape vegetation during the first 30 days after planting.

rebates.summary: Free sprinkler evaluations from Resource Central irrigation technicians for residential, commercial and HOA potable-water users, first come, first served.
A limited number of Resource Central Garden In A Box kits are discounted $25 each year for Wellington Water Utility customers.

backflow.summary: Backflow protection for a lawn sprinkler system requires a Town permit. The Town's Standard Design Criteria (2015, revised 2017) say required backflow assemblies must be tested at installation and re-tested every year.

other.summary: Town watering guidelines take precedence over HOA landscape enforcement; the Town notes Colorado law bars an HOA from fining a homeowner who follows local watering restrictions or guidelines, even if the lawn goes dormant.
Call 811 or 800-922-1987 before digging; the Town notes it is free and required by law.

permit_office.name: Town of Estes Park Building Safety (Community Development), contracted to SAFEbuilt
permit_office.summary: Since 2020 the Town has contracted its building division services through SAFEbuilt; permits are applied for through the Community Connect portal, and contractors need a Town license (970-577-3735, building@estes.org).

row_permit.summary: Public Works requires a Right-of-Way Work Permit for any work in the right-of-way, including excavation, culverts, driveways and sidewalks; the fee is $50 plus $200 for excavation in the asphalt roadway, and applications are due 5 to 30 days before excavation. Work in CDOT right-of-way also needs a CDOT permit.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's Permit Exemption List (2021 IRC) exempts sidewalks and driveways from building permits.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls are exempt up to 4 ft, measured from a point 8 ft downslope from the low-side finish grade to the high-side finish grade behind the wall, if the next uphill wall is at least twice the upper wall's height away and the wall supports no surcharge. Walls outside that exemption need a building permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Estes Park Water Division (Utilities)
water_provider.summary: The Water Division serves the Town's defined water service area and handles backflow regulation.

backflow.summary: The Town generally requires reduced pressure zone (RPZ) backflow assemblies on irrigation lines; tests must be done by an ABPA- or ASSE-certified technician and submitted to BSI Online. Single-family homes are not monitored, but the Town strongly encourages owners to protect hazards with an assembly and test it annually.

other.summary: Per the Town's grading permit application (rev. 2011, linked on the current Building Forms page), a grading permit is required for cuts of 2 ft or more, fills of 1 ft or more or 50 cubic yards or more, cut slopes of 67% or more or fill slopes of 20% or more, or any change in stormwater flow toward the right-of-way or a neighbor.
All work in the right-of-way requires a free locate request to 811 (800-922-1987) first.

permit_office.name: City of Longmont Building Inspection Division (Building Services)
permit_office.summary: Permits are reviewed and issued at the Building Inspection Division office, Development Services Center, 385 Kimbark St.; (303) 651-8332.

row_permit.summary: A Work in the Right-of-Way permit is required before curb, gutter, ramp, driveway or sidewalk repairs or new installations, street cuts, and utility or tree work in the public right-of-way. It requires a certificate of insurance naming the City ($350,000 per person / $1,000,000 per occurrence) and costs $25 for initial review plus $30 for up to three inspections.

flatwork_permit.summary: The City's examples of work requiring a building permit list 'Patios, sunrooms, decks, and pergolas' under additions; driveways and sidewalks on private property are not addressed, and permit questions go to Building Services at (303) 651-8332.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 48 inches require a building permit.

water_provider.name: City of Longmont Water Utilities
water_provider.summary: The City provides water within city limits. Left Hand Water District generally serves areas southwest, south and southeast of the City's service area, and Longs Peak Water District serves areas northwest, north and northeast.

watering_rules.summary: Longmont remains at a Mild Drought Response Level (unchanged since May): reductions are voluntary for residents and there are no mandatory watering days. The City recommends not watering between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m., using cycle-and-soak, considering one less watering day per week, and turning off automatic irrigation on October 1.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (page last modified 2026-08-18)

new_sod.summary: Since January 1, 2026, landscape plans for new development and redevelopment must use drought-tolerant or native vegetation as the primary ground cover, and nonfunctional turf (including artificial turf), such as strips between sidewalk and curb, is prohibited.

rebates.summary: Bill-credit rebate for efficient irrigation equipment, including smart irrigation controllers, for City of Longmont water customers; apply within 45 days of purchase with proof of purchase (amounts are not listed on the page).
Listed on the City's water conservation page as a new program for removing lawn and replacing it with water-wise landscaping, applied for through Resource Central.
Free sprinkler system evaluation through Resource Central, including a custom watering schedule.

backflow.summary: Testable backflow assemblies require at least annual testing, with results reported to the City. Testers must be ABPA- or ASSE-certified and submit through the online Backflow Assembly Test & Maintenance Report or by email to backflow@longmontcolorado.gov; property owners own the devices on their property.

other.summary: Municipal Code 14.04.490 defines water waste, including excessive runoff into streets and failing to repair broken sprinkler heads or irrigation lines in a timely manner; fines can follow ignored warnings.
A Forestry permit signed by the Public Works and Natural Resources director or designee is required to prune, remove or treat a City-owned tree or to plant a tree in the City right-of-way.
Property owners are responsible for the water service line from the property line to the house foundation.

permit_office.name: City of Boulder Planning & Development Services

row_permit.summary: Work in the public right-of-way, including curb cuts, street cuts and sidewalks, needs a Right-of-Way permit from Planning & Development Services. Only a right-of-way licensed contractor may apply, and licensing requires insurance, workers' compensation and a surety bond.

flatwork_permit.summary: Private sidewalks, patios and driveways don't need a building permit if they are no more than 30 inches above grade, not over a basement or story below, and not part of an accessible route. Exempt work must still meet building, zoning and engineering rules, and sites in a floodplain, wetland or historic district may need other approvals.

retaining_wall.summary: A retaining wall is exempt only if it is no more than 3 feet tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall. Taller walls, and any wall supporting a surcharge, need a permit.

water_provider.name: City of Boulder Utilities

watering_rules.summary: Boulder remains in a voluntary Drought Watch with no mandatory restrictions. Lawns should be watered no more than 2 days a week: single-family even addresses on Sunday and Thursday, odd addresses on Wednesday and Saturday, and all others on Tuesday and Friday. A permanent rule bans watering landscaping with city water from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., May 1 through September 30; drip systems and hand watering with a shut-off nozzle are exempt.
watering_rules.as_of: May 1, 2026 release; Drought Watch confirmed in the Oct. 1, 2026 update

new_sod.summary: Under Drought Watch, new landscapes may still be installed and watered, and new plant material is exempt from the 10 a.m.-6 p.m. ban for 30 days after installation. Projects that require a landscape plan (new development or redevelopment) on lots with 3 or fewer units may have turf on no more than 25% of the lot or 1,000 sq ft, whichever is less, and Kentucky bluegrass, tall fescue and similar cool-season grasses are allowed only in functional turf areas.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow irrigation audit (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free sprinkler irrigation audits for City of Boulder water customers while supplies last.
Up to $750 in discounts toward converting at least 200 sq ft of turf to water-wise gardens while supplies last, supported by HB-1151 funds.
Residents enrolled in Boulder's Food Tax Rebate program get $100 off a Garden-in-a-Box kit. Other income-qualified residents can ask about it at bouldersaveswater@bouldercolorado.gov.

backflow.summary: Single-unit homes and duplexes are generally exempt from annual backflow testing unless they have a dedicated irrigation or fire line off the main, an auxiliary water source, or another identified hazard. A home with a separate metered irrigation account must install an approved assembly and have it tested every year by an ABPA- or ASSE-certified tester, who submits the results through the city's Backflow Web Portal within 10 days.

other.summary: Owners must keep the sidewalk next to their property in good repair (B.R.C. 8-2-6). Under the city's annual sidewalk repair program, owners pay up to half the cost, capped at $450 per year for single-family homes.
Owners are also responsible for some upkeep of the right-of-way next to their property, such as clearing snow from sidewalks and mowing grass.

permit_office.name: City of Lafayette Building Division (Planning & Building Department)
permit_office.note: The 2024 I-codes and 2026 NEC took effect August 1, 2026.

row_permit.summary: Any work in the public right-of-way, including new work on or repairs to concrete sidewalk, curb and gutter, needs a Right-of-Way permit from Public Works through the City's online portal. Every contractor on the permit must hold a City of Lafayette contractor license and a $5,000 street-cut bond.

flatwork_permit.summary: The 2026 Lafayette Building Code (Sec. 105.2) exempts sidewalks and driveways from a building permit if they are no more than 30 inches above adjacent grade, not over a basement or story below, and not part of an accessible route. Patios are not listed separately.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls under 3 feet tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, are exempt unless they support a surcharge or hold back Class I, II or III liquids. Walls 3 feet or taller need a building permit.

water_provider.name: City of Lafayette Public Works - Water
water_provider.note: The City's watering restrictions also apply to properties outside city limits that are served by Lafayette water.

watering_rules.summary: Lafayette has been in Stage 1 drought response since April 10, 2026 and strongly encourages watering with irrigation systems no more than 2 days a week. Year-round rules (LMC 120-13) ban watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., watering more than 3 days a week (the week runs Sunday through Saturday), runoff onto pavement, and hosing down paved areas; hand watering with an automatic shut-off nozzle is allowed.
watering_rules.as_of: Stage 1 effective April 10, 2026

new_sod.summary: The City discourages installing new sod during drought, and any irrigation must follow the restrictions in place. Newly planted xeric landscaping, or reseeding with native or dryland grass, can get a 30-day exemption from the watering-day limit (but not the 10 a.m.-6 p.m. ban) if approved in advance through droughtoutreach@lafayetteco.gov.

rebates.program: Outdoor Water Efficiency Rebates (City of Lafayette)
rebates.summary: Homeowners get a utility-bill credit of $3 per rotary or high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle (10 to 50 nozzles, once per 10 years) and up to $50 for drip equipment. A Resource Central Slow the Flow report is required, and items must have been bought within the last 6 months.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow sprinkler assessment (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free 75-minute sprinkler system evaluation for Lafayette residents during irrigation season.

rebates.program: Smart controller and rain sensor installation (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Rachio smart controllers and Rain Bird rain sensors are installed at no cost for eligible City water customers while supplies last. A Slow the Flow evaluation is required first.
For at least 200 sq ft of healthy lawn, up to $750 in discounts toward lawn removal service, or free Garden In A Box kits if you remove the lawn yourself.
City discounts on low-water garden kits are applied at checkout while limited funds last. Income-qualified residents can request a discount code from sustainability@lafayetteco.gov.

backflow.summary: Backflow assemblies on non-single-family residential and commercial water accounts must be tested every year, with irrigation assemblies due by May 31; results go to the City's contractor, BSI Online. Failed tests must be reported within 24 hours, and a missed deadline brings a $250 fee per assembly plus water shutoff; the City generally requires a vacuum breaker on irrigation systems.

other.summary: The City maintains all sidewalks, curbs, gutters and curbwalks (LMC 105-31).
The property owner is responsible for the water service line from the meter pit, which is usually just inside the right-of-way, to the home or irrigation system.

Anyone who builds, alters or repairs buildings, structures or equipment for pay needs a City contractor license (2026 Lafayette Building Code Sec. 119.2). License classes include concrete (Class SCC, which covers patios, slabs, driveways and sidewalks), irrigation (Class SI) and right-of-way work (Class ROW).

permit_office.name: City of Louisville Building Safety (Department of Planning and Building Safety)

row_permit.summary: Construction or utility work in a City street, sidewalk or easement needs a right-of-way or easement permit from Public Works before work starts. The fee is a $75 base plus $0.30 per linear foot of curb, gutter, sidewalk or driveway ramp, and all fees double if work starts first. Subcontractors must be licensed with the City, disturbed sidewalks and landscaping must be restored, and work carries a 2-year warranty; LMC 12.08.010 separately requires a permit to build or rebuild any sidewalk, curb or gutter.

flatwork_permit.summary: The City's permit table says pouring an uncovered concrete patio needs no permit. Driveway repair and sidewalk repair may need one; contact Public Works first.

retaining_wall.summary: A retaining wall under 48 inches from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, with no surcharge, doesn't need a building permit. Walls over 48 inches, and any wall with a surcharge, need stamped engineered plans, and the City's permit table says to check with the Planning Department first (Minor Permit: Retaining Wall).

water_provider.name: City of Louisville Public Works - Water and Sewer
water_provider.note: Drinking water comes from South Boulder Creek and the Colorado and Fraser Rivers and is treated at two City plants.

watering_rules.summary: Louisville has no mandatory watering restrictions in 2026 and is asking for voluntary conservation. The City asked residents to keep sprinklers off until mid-to-late May, keep water off pavement, and end lawn watering by October 1; hand watering of trees, shrubs and gardens can continue.
watering_rules.as_of: Updated 09/29/2026

new_sod.summary: For 2026 the City strongly recommended that residents hold off on establishing a new lawn and consider drought-tolerant landscaping instead.

rebates.program: Garden In A Box (Resource Central, in partnership with the City)
rebates.summary: Low-water garden kits offered through Resource Central in partnership with the City. The City lists no discount amount.

rebates.program: Slow the Flow sprinkler evaluation (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free sprinkler evaluations offered with the City.
Incentives for replacing lawn with water-wise landscaping. The City lists no dollar amount.

backflow.summary: City design criteria require a backflow preventer on residential irrigation systems, and installing one needs a minor plumbing permit. City code (LMC 13.08.180) requires backflow assemblies on identified hazardous cross-connections to be tested at installation and every year after, at the customer's cost; the City uses Backflow Solutions, Inc. (BSI) to track assemblies.

other.summary: The City's permit table says an irrigation system needs a permit (MEP single-trade: new sewer, water or irrigation tap).
Before digging for right-of-way work, call Colorado 811 (1-800-922-1987) for utility locates.

permit_office.name: Town of Superior Building Department (operated by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.note: Applications are filed online through Community Core. Building Department phone: 303-381-2028.

row_permit.summary: Any construction or excavation in the public right-of-way needs a Town right-of-way permit, and curbs, gutters, sidewalks and driveways there must meet the Town's standard street specifications (Sec. 11-2-30). Apply through Public Works & Utilities' 'Right-Of-Way & Utility Construction' form; the Town's design standards waive the letter of credit or cash deposit for residential sidewalk and driveway repairs and replacements.

flatwork_permit.summary: Superior's 2026 residential code amendments (Sec. 18-8-20) change only the IRC permit exemptions for sheds, fences and decks, leaving the IRC exemption for sidewalks and driveways in place. The Town's list of projects that need permits doesn't include patios or driveways, but the Town says the list may not be complete.
flatwork_permit.note: Superior amends IRC R105.2 exemptions by number (#1, #2, #10 and a new #11). The sidewalk/driveway exemption is IRC R105.2 item 5, which the Town leaves unchanged.

retaining_wall.summary: The Town's permit guidance says retaining walls over 4 feet tall need a building permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Superior Public Works & Utilities - Water Division
water_provider.note: Most raw water comes from the Upper Colorado River Basin through Northern Water. Reclaimed water irrigates parks and commercial areas.

watering_rules.summary: Superior is at Stage I (Watch) of its June 2026 Drought Mitigation Plan, which asks residents to voluntarily water 2 days a week: single-family even addresses on Saturday and Wednesday, odd addresses on Sunday and Thursday, and other residential properties such as multifamily and HOAs on Monday and Friday. On Oct. 2, 2026 the Town asked residents to voluntarily stop lawn watering for the rest of the year; these requests are not mandatory or enforced.
watering_rules.as_of: June 2026 Drought Mitigation Plan; Oct. 2, 2026 update

new_sod.summary: Under the Drought Mitigation Plan, residents at Stage I are encouraged to put off installing new sod, seed and landscaping until the drought ends. At Stages II-IV, residents are to forgo such installations.

rebates.program: Water Efficiency Rebate Program (Town of Superior)
rebates.summary: Homeowners upgrading an existing home get utility-bill credits: $3 per rotary or high-efficiency nozzle (10 to 50 nozzles, $30-$150), up to $100 for a WaterSense smart sprinkler controller, up to $50 for drip equipment, and up to $50 per rain barrel ($100 total). Credits are first-come, first-served while funds last.
Up to $750 in incentives for removing at least 200 sq ft of lawn, through discounted removal or discounted xeric plants, first-come, first-served.

rebates.program: Free sprinkler audits - Slow the Flow (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free 75-minute outdoor sprinkler evaluation during irrigation season.

rebates.program: Free smart controllers and rain sensors (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Free Rachio smart controllers and Rain Bird rain sensors, installation included, first-come, first-served.
Low-water garden kits, with a limited number of Town-funded discounts for residents.

backflow.summary: The Town's backflow and cross-connection program covers non-single-family connections: those customers must test backflow devices every year and complete cross-connection surveys. The Town says this mainly affects business owners and property managers.

other.summary: The adjacent owner must maintain the sidewalk and parkway, including the landscaping, and clear snow and ice from the sidewalk within 24 hours. The Town may repair a hazardous sidewalk and bill the owner (Sec. 11-1-20, 11-1-40).
Superior began licensing contractors on Oct. 13, 2025. Specialty licenses require a Colorado certificate of good standing and insurance and cover trades including concrete, fencing and 'sprinklers'.

permit_office.name: Town of Lyons Building Department (contracted to SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.note: Permits are filed through Community Core, and a $50 Town of Lyons contractor license is required to pull one. The 2024 ICC codes took effect July 1, 2026.

row_permit.summary: Street cuts and access work in the Town right-of-way need a Town of Lyons Right of Way Permit ($100) with a traffic control plan, approved by the Director of Utilities and Engineering. Work must follow the Town Engineer's encroachment requirements, a bond may be held until the Town Engineer inspects it, and public improvements carry a one-year guarantee.

flatwork_permit.summary: Lyons' 2026 residential code amendments (LMC 18-3-40, Ord. 1211) delete the IRC permit exemption for sidewalks and driveways, along with the fence exemption, so that work is no longer listed as permit-exempt. Check with the Building Department before pouring.
flatwork_permit.note: The code deletes IRC R105.2 Exceptions #2 and #5 by number. In the IRC list, #2 is fences and #5 is sidewalks and driveways (see the IRC exemption list the Town of Nederland posts: https://www.nederlandco.org/DocumentCenter/View/459/Work-Exempt-for-Permit-from-IRC). The Lyons building page confirms fence permits are now required.

retaining_wall.summary: Lyons' 2026 amendments don't change the IRC retaining-wall exemption: walls no more than 4 feet tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, are exempt unless they support a surcharge. Taller or surcharged walls need a permit.
retaining_wall.note: Lyons amends IRC R105.2 by exception number and leaves #3, the retaining-wall exemption, in place. The 4-ft wording is the IRC text, as shown in the IRC exemption list the Town of Nederland posts: https://www.nederlandco.org/DocumentCenter/View/459/Work-Exempt-for-Permit-from-IRC

water_provider.name: Town of Lyons Water Utility (water supplied and treated by the City of Longmont)

watering_rules.summary: The Town posts voluntary guidelines rather than a mandatory schedule: water lawns deeply twice a week in the early morning, and don't water between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated guidance page (checked Oct. 2026)

new_sod.summary: Town guidance says to avoid installing landscaping during the hottest months, especially in dry years, and to use drought-resistant turf, xeric plants and drip irrigation where possible.

rebates.summary: Pre-planned xeric garden kits. The Town's page says this year's discounts come from the St. Vrain and Left Hand Water Conservancy District.
Free sprinkler consultation of about 90 minutes to improve irrigation efficiency. Book at 303-999-3824.
Cash incentives to remove turf and switch to water-wise landscaping.

backflow.summary: A backflow preventer on a commercial or multi-family connection must be tested every year by a State-certified tester (LMC 13-6-60). Passing results go to the Utilities Director or Town Hall by July 15, and late reports can bring fines or water disconnection (LMC 13-6-100).

other.summary: Owners must maintain the right-of-way next to their property. Sidewalks must stay passable, with vegetation trimmed to 7 feet and snow and ice removed within 24 hours after it has stopped falling for 4 hours, and grass and weeds, including in the strip between the property line and curb, must stay under 6 inches (LMC 7-2-140, 7-2-150).
It is unlawful to leave sod, earth, sand, gravel, concrete or other construction material on any street, alley or public place (LMC 7-2-80).
Permitted work on a property in the floodplain also needs a Town floodplain development permit. Fence permits are required as of July 1, 2026 under the Wildfire Resiliency Code.

permit_office.name: Town of Nederland Building, Planning & Zoning Department (Community Planner)
permit_office.note: Building and right-of-way permit applications go to planner@nederlandco.org. The Town says it is governed by the 2024 ICC codes and uses SAFEbuilt for some plan review.

row_permit.summary: Work in the Town right-of-way needs a permit. The Right-of-Way & Excavating and Blasting Permit Application (rev. 6/2024) lists a $125 right-of-way fee, a $175 excavation fee, a $1,000 security deposit for right-of-way work, proof of liability insurance, and warranties of 6 months for dirt and 1 year for concrete or asphalt. New driveways that access a public street need a culvert at least 18 inches in diameter, approved by Public Works with the building permit (NMC 11-21, 11-23).

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town's posted IRC list of work exempt from permits includes sidewalks and driveways. In residential zones, though, an excavation permit is required unless the dig is on private property, doesn't affect the right-of-way, moves less than 50 cubic yards, and is outside floodplain and wetlands (NMC 11-42).

retaining_wall.summary: Under the Town's posted IRC exempt-work list, retaining walls no more than 4 feet tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, are exempt unless they support a surcharge. Taller or surcharged walls need a permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Nederland Utilities Department (Town water plant)

watering_rules.summary: The Town's Utilities page doesn't post a watering schedule. Under the Municipal Code (NMC 13-71, 13-72), the Town Administrator can limit lawn-watering days and hours when needed, with Board of Trustees approval.
watering_rules.as_of: No 2026 schedule posted (checked Oct. 2026)

new_sod.summary: When conservation measures are in effect, the Director of Public Works may issue special permits, for a fee, to water newly sodded lawns daily for up to 14 consecutive days and newly seeded lawns for up to 25 consecutive days (NMC 13-73).

backflow.summary: Commercial users, and residential users with hazards such as a well or other auxiliary supply, internal cross-connections or a fire system, must install an approved backflow device. Required devices must be tested at installation and at least once a year by a certified cross-connection control technician, who sends the results to the Director of Public Works (NMC 13-198, 13-200, 13-202).

other.summary: Owners must clear snow, ice and debris from the sidewalk next to their property within 12 hours of the last accumulation (NMC 11-1).

permit_office.name: Boulder County Community Planning & Permitting (reviews plans and inspects work in Jamestown under an agreement with the Town)

row_permit.summary: The Town of Jamestown issues driveway permits; contact the Town Clerk. Under Ordinance 7 (2004), a new residence needs a driveway permit before work starts: a $200 fee, Fire Chief approval of the site, a driveway at least 12 feet wide (14 feet clear), a maximum 12% grade (14% for up to 200 feet), and an erosion-control plan.

flatwork_permit.summary: Boulder County, which reviews and inspects building work in Jamestown, exempts sidewalks and driveways from a building permit if they are no more than 30 inches above adjacent grade, not over a basement or story below, not part of an accessible route, and not subject to a grading permit.

retaining_wall.summary: Boulder County exempts retaining walls no more than 4 feet tall, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless they support a surcharge or hold back Class I, II or IIIA liquids. Other walls need a permit.

water_provider.name: Town of Jamestown municipal water system (Town water treatment plant)

watering_rules.summary: The Town's water page doesn't post a watering schedule. The Waterworks Ordinance (Ord. 1, Series 2015, Sec. 20) requires hoses on the system to have nozzles or sprinklers and requires customers to follow any watering or sprinkling ban posted by the Town or Water Plant Operator; violations can lead to water shutoff.
watering_rules.as_of: Ordinance 1, Series 2015; no 2026 ban posted on the Town water page (checked Oct. 2026)

backflow.summary: The Waterworks Ordinance requires a backflow prevention device on every external faucet, and an approved backflow device on any connection the Town Water Engineer or operators consider a contamination risk, under the Town's Cross Connection Plan (available from the Town Clerk). It doesn't set a testing schedule.

other.summary: The owner is responsible for the water service line from the curb box to the building, and repairs need a Water Service Line Repair Application, Agreement and Permit from the Town Clerk.
Floodplain development permits are issued by the Town of Jamestown.

permit_office.name: Town of Ward (contact the Town directly)
permit_office.note: Boulder County issues permits only in unincorporated areas (it also reviews Jamestown permits under an agreement) and sends town properties to the town. Its building contacts page lists the Town of Ward as 303-459-9273 and townofward@gmail.com and gives no Town website; its towns directory lists 303-459-3358.

permit_office.name: City and County of Denver Community Planning and Development (CPD), Development Services
permit_office.summary: CPD reviews and issues building and zoning permits for single-family and duplex projects; simple projects such as most porches, patios, decks, sheds and fences can get same-day review at the walk-through counter (questions: 720-865-2710).

row_permit.summary: Any construction in Denver's public right-of-way, such as changing curb and gutter, sidewalks, driveways or curb ramps, requires review and approval by DOTI Transportation Engineering, and DOTI's Encroachments group (720-865-3003, DOTI.ER@denvergov.org) issues permits for construction work in the right-of-way. ROW construction, street-cut and street-occupancy permits are filed online through E-Permits, and a Street Occupancy Permit is always required in addition to the construction or street-cut permit.

flatwork_permit.summary: Section 130.3 of the 2025 Denver Building Code exempts flatwork (hardscape) such as sidewalks, ramps and driveways from building permits when the walking surface is no more than 30 inches above grade, not over a basement or story below, and not part of an accessible route. Covered patios still need both a zoning and a building permit, and a new or modified driveway connection or curb cut is reviewed by city transportation engineers.

retaining_wall.summary: Denver requires a zoning permit for any wall over 12 inches high, including retaining walls, and the 2025 Denver Building Code exempts retaining walls from building permits only up to 4 feet total height (bottom of footing to top of wall, including any fence on top) and only if they do not support a surcharge. CPD's residential checklist requires structural calculations for retaining walls that retain more than 24 inches of soil or are over 4 feet from the bottom of the footing, and masonry or retaining walls over 6 feet get engineering plan review.

water_provider.name: Denver Water
water_provider.summary: Denver Water serves the city of Denver and many surrounding suburbs.

watering_rules.summary: Under Denver Water's Stage 1 drought (declared March 25, 2026), lawns could be watered only two assigned days a week (single-family even addresses Sunday/Thursday, odd addresses Wednesday/Saturday, all other customers Tuesday/Friday) and only between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m. Since Oct. 1, 2026, all lawn watering and spray irrigation is prohibited until further Board action, while trees, shrubs, perennials and vegetables may be watered any day by hand-held hose with a shut-off nozzle or by drip.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 declared Mar. 25, 2026; lawn/spray irrigation ban from Oct. 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: During the 2026 drought, Denver Water's Watering Establishment Permit allowed watering of new bluegrass seed, sod, trees or plants for up to 3 weeks and new native grass seed for up to 8 weeks, with watering rules and drought pricing still applying. As of Oct. 1, 2026, Denver Water no longer issues these permits except for Lead Replacement Program, mainline pipe replacement and Certificate of Occupancy projects.

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Customers who get a water bill from Denver Water or a qualifying provider can get up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 eligible rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain) that replace existing heads; one rebate per residence per 10 years, applied for online within 90 days of purchase and subject to available funds.

rebates.program: Turfgrass removal discount (Denver Water with Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Residential customers could get up to $750 off 2026 turfgrass removal services; all 2026 discounts were allocated by March 28, 2026 and Resource Central is no longer accepting applications.
Eligible Denver Water residential customers get $25 off Resource Central water-wise plant kits during the spring and fall sales, while the limited discounts last.

backflow.summary: Denver Water requires backflow prevention assemblies to be tested by a certified tester at installation and every year after, with test reports sent to crossconnectioncontrol@denverwater.org. Irrigation systems must use a reduced-pressure assembly or pressure vacuum breaker, and irrigation assemblies are tested May through September when the water is turned on.

other.summary: Since voters created the Sidewalk Enterprise Fund in 2022, DOTI builds and repairs sidewalks with a fee every Denver property owner pays (2026: $150 base charge plus $3.50 per foot of frontage over 230 feet); repairs are scheduled from 3-1-1 damage reports, not on demand.

Sprinkler system damage caused by the city's sidewalk repair work can be reported through Denver's online service hub ('Damage Caused by Concrete Repair'), the sidewalk hotline 720-337-6380, or sidewalks@denvergov.org.

CPD's permitting checklist says curb cuts and access on state highways such as Federal Blvd, Colfax Ave and Colorado Blvd need CDOT access permits, and lists Colorado 811 (1-800-922-1987) for marking underground utilities before digging.

permit_office.name: City and County of Broomfield Building Division (Community Development)
permit_office.summary: The Building Division issues building permits, reviews plans, inspects and enforces building codes (303-438-6370); fence permits go through the Planning Division and right-of-way work through the Engineering Division.

row_permit.summary: Any construction in Broomfield's public right-of-way requires a Public Private Improvement Permit (PPIP) from the City Engineer (engineeringpermits@broomfield.org, 303-438-6380), whose fee schedule includes drive cuts and curb/gutter by the linear foot. Contractors must hold a Broomfield Contractor's License and a certificate of insurance, processing typically takes 5-10 business days after a complete submittal, and a preconstruction meeting is required.

flatwork_permit.summary: Broomfield's homeowner guidance says on-grade patios do not require a permit and do not need to meet setbacks, but pouring a new driveway or doing other flatwork may require a Public Private Improvement Permit from the Engineering Division.

retaining_wall.summary: Broomfield's Building Division lists retaining walls among projects that require a building permit, and the submittal for a retaining wall more than 3 feet tall must include plans, a site plan and an engineer-stamped report.

water_provider.name: City and County of Broomfield Water Utilities

watering_rules.summary: Broomfield's Water Use Ordinance (in effect since Jan. 1, 2025) allows lawn watering no more than three days a week (even addresses Monday/Wednesday/Friday, odd addresses Tuesday/Thursday/Sunday) and only between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m. Broomfield remains in a Drought Watch, reaffirmed Aug. 25, 2026, which asks residents to voluntarily cut lawn watering to two days a week.
watering_rules.as_of: Aug. 25, 2026 status update

new_sod.summary: Broomfield says residents installing new seed or sod this year can get an exception to water as needed to establish it, but must contact the City and County first. The Water Use Ordinance also limits installation of new sod or seed when City Council declares a drought.

rebates.program: Irrigation controller and sprinkler nozzle rebates
rebates.summary: Broomfield offers rebates to residents, HOAs and commercial properties for replacing outdated irrigation controllers and sprinkler nozzles with high-efficiency models; amounts are not posted (720-557-1336, conservation@broomfield.org).
Rebates are offered for installing rain barrels; the amount is not posted on the page.
Broomfield does not pay residents a rebate to remove grass, but partners with Resource Central to offer residents a turf-removal discount of up to $750.
Broomfield residents get $25 off Resource Central low-water plant kits.
Free outdoor sprinkler evaluation that identifies watering changes to lower the bill.
Pays $2.50 per square foot to non-residential and multifamily water customers, including HOA common areas; single-family homes are not eligible.

backflow.summary: Broomfield runs its cross-connection (backflow) program with Backflow Solutions, Inc.; testers must keep credentials current on BSI Online and submit test reports there, with a $14.95 filing fee per report. The notice does not state a testing interval for residential irrigation assemblies.

other.summary: Broomfield requires a fence permit, processed by the Planning Division, for new, replacement and relocated fences.
The Water Use Ordinance requires leaking sprinkler systems to be repaired within 10 days and bars letting water pool on hard surfaces or flow down gutters.

permit_office.name: City of Arvada Building Services
permit_office.summary: Building Services (8101 Ralston Road, 720-898-7620) issues residential permits electronically through eTRAKiT (ArvadaPermits.org).

row_permit.summary: Work in Arvada's right-of-way needs a Right of Way Permit from the Engineering Division, applied for online; flatwork replacement permits (curb and gutter, detached walks, crosspans, ADA ramps, chase drains) are issued only to contractors with a current Arvada Municipal General Contractor license. Applications need a Colorado 811 locate confirmation number plus site and traffic control plans, curb cuts require a pre-construction meeting, and concrete replacement carries a two-year warranty.

retaining_wall.summary: Arvada requires a building permit for retaining walls over 4 feet measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, and for any wall supporting a surcharge regardless of height; applications need a soils report and engineer-stamped drawings. Walls over 4 feet also need a variance or minor modification approved by Planning before the permit is issued.

water_provider.name: City of Arvada water utility
water_provider.summary: Most Arvada residents get water from the City; some areas are served by Ralston Valley Water & Sanitation District, Valley Water District, North Table Mountain Water, Consolidated Mutual Water Company or Denver Water.

watering_rules.summary: Arvada has been in a Stage 1 drought since April 15, 2026 (following Denver Water's stages): lawn watering two days a week (single-family even addresses Sunday/Thursday, odd Wednesday/Saturday, all others Tuesday/Friday) and no outdoor watering 10 a.m.-6 p.m., with trees, shrubs, gardens and flowers allowed any day by hand or drip outside those hours. The rules apply to City of Arvada water customers, with fines of $100, $250 and $500 after a warning.
watering_rules.as_of: Page updated June 17, 2026 (Stage 1 effective Apr. 15, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Under Arvada's Stage 1 rules, new grass seed or sod is allowed but must follow the two-day schedule from June through August, and the City recommends avoiding new grass in those months. The 21-day establishment variance ended May 31, 2026 and will not be offered in fall 2026.

rebates.summary: City of Arvada water customers can buy discounted water-wise garden kits while supplies last; spring orders open in March and late-summer orders in June.
Many City of Arvada water customers are eligible for discounts on having a section of lawn cut, removed and composted.
In-person sprinkler inspection by Resource Central with a customized watering schedule, for City of Arvada water customers (not HOAs).

backflow.summary: Arvada notes that all backflow prevention assemblies must be inspected and tested annually; the City mails annual testing notices and registered testers submit results through its online platform, SAMS (backflow program: 720-898-7793).

other.summary: Arvada property owners and occupants must maintain the area out to the street, including sidewalks, curbs and gutters, clear snow and ice from adjoining sidewalks within 24 hours after snowfall stops, and keep tree branches 10 feet above sidewalks and 14 feet above the street.
Off-street parking spaces and driveways in Arvada must be asphalt or concrete, and new or replacement fences require a permit.

permit_office.name: City of Wheat Ridge Building Division (Building and Inspection Services)
permit_office.summary: Questions: (303) 235-2855, option 1; zoning questions go to the Planner of the Day.

row_permit.summary: Any work in Wheat Ridge's right-of-way needs a ROW Excavation Permit or ROW Occupancy Permit from Public Works (curb, gutter and sidewalk work is not covered by a building permit), applied for through the City's OpenGov portal with a traffic control plan. The applicant needs a current Wheat Ridge Municipal Contractor License (Class A covers curb, gutter and sidewalk construction) backed by a $10,000 cash bond or approved performance bond, and work on Sheridan, Wadsworth, Kipling or Ward Rd also needs a CDOT permit.

retaining_wall.summary: Wheat Ridge requires a building permit for retaining walls over 4 feet high or supporting a surcharge.

water_provider.name: Multiple providers: Denver Water, Consolidated Mutual Water Company, Valley Water District and Wheat Ridge Water District
water_provider.summary: Water lines are owned by special districts, and Denver Water is the main supplier for most of them; Wheat Ridge Water District serves most of the city east of Independence Court plus the area south of I-70 between Carr and Garrison, and Consolidated Mutual serves other parts of Wheat Ridge.

watering_rules.summary: All four Wheat Ridge water providers follow Stage 1 drought rules: lawn watering two days a week (single-family even addresses Sunday/Thursday, odd Wednesday/Saturday, all others Tuesday/Friday) and none from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with trees, shrubs and gardens allowed any day by hand or drip outside those hours. Wheat Ridge Water District has prohibited all lawn watering and lawn spray irrigation beginning Oct. 1, 2026.
watering_rules.as_of: City page updated Apr. 13, 2026; WRWD lawn-watering ban from Oct. 1, 2026

new_sod.summary: Wheat Ridge's restrictions page says new grass seed or sod is subject to the two-day watering schedule from June through August, and Wheat Ridge Water District says it will not grant any variance for new seed or sod.

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Customers of Denver Water or a qualifying provider (the list includes Valley Water District and Wheat Ridge Water District, but not Consolidated Mutual) can get up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 eligible rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain) that replace existing heads; one rebate per residence per 10 years, applied for online within 90 days of purchase and subject to available funds.

backflow.summary: Backflow testing is run by each water provider: Consolidated Mutual requires assemblies to be tested every year after installation, failed tests reported within 24 hours and fixed within 10 days, and accepts reports only through its portal (sprybackflow.cmwc.net). Denver Water requires annual tests by a certified tester, with reports emailed to crossconnectioncontrol@denverwater.org.

other.summary: Wheat Ridge lists exterior irrigation systems among the projects that require a building permit.
Water and sanitary sewer lines in Wheat Ridge are owned by special districts, which require their own permits for work on those lines.

permit_office.name: City of Lakewood permit counter (building permits and inspections)
permit_office.summary: Lakewood handles permitting and inspections through eTRAKiT and the permit counter at 470 S. Allison Pkwy (PermitCounter@LakewoodCO.gov, 303-987-7500).

row_permit.summary: Lakewood permits and inspects concrete work in the public way, including sidewalks, curb and gutter, curb ramps, driveways and driveway aprons, and only contractors with a Class D Municipal registration may take permits for right-of-way work (the Concrete 5A class does not cover the public way). For right-of-way permit questions, the City says to contact an engineering plans reviewer at 303-987-7500.

flatwork_permit.summary: Lakewood's list of permit exemptions says private walks and driveways no more than 30 inches above grade, not over a basement or story below and not part of an accessible route, do not need a building permit; patio covers do require one.

retaining_wall.summary: In Lakewood, retaining walls up to 30 inches tall (measured from grade to the top of the wall) are exempt unless they support a surcharge or impound flammable liquids; retaining walls taller than 30 inches require a permit.

water_provider.name: Multiple providers (nearly 20), most buying water from Denver Water
water_provider.summary: Lakewood's provider list includes Consolidated Mutual Water Company, Denver Water, the City's own Lakewood Water and Sewer Utility, and the Green Mountain, Alameda, Bancroft-Clover, Bear Creek, Bonvue and Lakehurst water and sanitation districts, among others; the City's My Neighborhood tool shows the provider for an address.

watering_rules.summary: Most Lakewood water providers follow Denver Water's Stage 1 drought rules: lawn watering two days a week by address, only between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m.; the City's Aug. 26 update says lawn watering and all spray irrigation are prohibited after Sept. 30, 2026, while trees and plants may still be watered by hand or drip. Some providers may set stricter rules, so residents should confirm with their own provider.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 Drought page, latest update Aug. 26, 2026

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Customers of Denver Water or a qualifying provider serving Lakewood (the list includes the City of Lakewood and the Alameda, Bancroft-Clover, Bonvue, Green Mountain and Lakehurst water and sanitation districts, but not Consolidated Mutual) can get up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 eligible rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain) that replace existing heads; one rebate per residence per 10 years, applied for online within 90 days of purchase and subject to available funds.

backflow.summary: Backflow testing is run by each water provider: Consolidated Mutual requires assemblies to be tested every year after installation and accepts reports only through its portal (sprybackflow.cmwc.net), and Denver Water requires annual tests by a certified tester with reports emailed to crossconnectioncontrol@denverwater.org.

other.summary: Lakewood lists fences, patio covers and retaining walls over 30 inches among work that requires a permit, and plumbing, electrical or mechanical permits are still needed for related work on otherwise exempt items.

water_provider.name: City of Edgewater
water_provider.summary: Denver Water lists the City of Edgewater as a qualifying water provider for its rebates; Edgewater's own utility pages could not be opened to confirm further details.

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Customers billed by the City of Edgewater (a Denver Water qualifying provider) can get up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 eligible rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain) that replace existing heads; one rebate per residence per 10 years, applied for online within 90 days of purchase and subject to available funds.

permit_office.name: City of Golden Building Division
permit_office.summary: Contact: (303) 384-8151, building@cityofgolden.net.

row_permit.summary: All work in Golden's right-of-way requires a Right of Way permit from Public Works, applied for through the City's online portal; contractors must be registered with the City and show general liability insurance. Concrete pours must be inspected by a Public Works inspector scheduled at least one business day ahead, and a traffic control plan is required for any occupancy of streets, sidewalks, trails or alleys.

flatwork_permit.summary: Golden's Required Building Permits Guide lists patio and porch covers as needing a permit and landscaping as not needing one; it does not address on-grade patios, driveways or other flatwork and directs residents to the Building Division for anything unclear.

retaining_wall.summary: Golden requires a permit, with engineering, for retaining or landscape walls (individually or in combination) over 4 feet tall measured from the bottom of the footing. Walls 4 feet or less are exempt unless they support a surcharge or are on a corner lot or in a historic district.

water_provider.name: City of Golden Utilities Division

watering_rules.summary: Golden has been in Stage 1 drought since May 1, 2026; its Amended Stage 1 Drought Order (effective July 19, 2026, in force until Oct. 31, 2026 unless rescinded earlier) limits lawns, trees, shrubs and perennials to two irrigation events per Sunday-Saturday week per property, on days the customer chooses, between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m., and bans all outdoor irrigation, including hand and drip watering, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Potted plants and food gardens may be hand-watered any day within the 6 p.m.-10 a.m. window, and power washing hardscapes and hand-washing vehicles at home are prohibited.
watering_rules.as_of: Amended Stage 1 Drought Order, effective July 19, 2026 through Oct. 31, 2026

new_sod.summary: Golden's Amended Stage 1 order grants no exceptions for new sod, turfgrass installation, native plantings or turf establishment watering; new plantings stay on the two-events-per-week limit and the 6 p.m.-10 a.m. window. The temporary irrigation exemptions Golden normally offers for new seed, sod, native gardens, trees and shrubs are not available during declared drought stages.

rebates.summary: Residential: 50% of the pre-tax price of a qualifying smart controller, up to $200; applicants must be registered on AquaHawk, new construction is not eligible, and funding is first-come, first-served.
$4 per nozzle when replacing fixed spray nozzles with accepted rotary models, up to $200 for residential customers registered on AquaHawk.
Up to 50% of drip equipment costs, capped at $200 per household, for converting overhead spray irrigation to drip; new construction does not qualify.
Full pre-tax price of a qualifying rain sensor added to an existing controller, up to $50 for residential customers.

rebates.program: Lawn Replacement and Garden In A Box (Resource Central)
rebates.summary: Golden's water conservation page points residents to Resource Central's Lawn Replacement and Garden In A Box programs; no amounts are listed.

backflow.summary: Golden requires backflow prevention on irrigation connections (among other connections), and assemblies must be tested annually by a certified backflow tester with reports emailed to backflow@cityofgolden.net; failing to test can lead to termination of service.

other.summary: Connecting a lawn sprinkler system to the water supply (backflow) requires a Golden building permit, and fences over 7 feet tall or in a front yard, on a corner lot or in a historic district need a permit.
Golden's drought order requires leaks to be repaired within ten calendar days of City notice and bars irrigation water from pooling or running off into streets, sidewalks, gutters or storm drains.

water_provider.name: Wheat Ridge Water District
water_provider.summary: The district, which buys its water from Denver Water, lists the Town of Lakeside in its service area.

watering_rules.summary: Wheat Ridge Water District is a Denver Water distributor and says Denver Water's Stage 1 drought and watering rules apply to it: lawn watering only on two assigned days a week (by even, odd or other address type) and only before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m., with hand or drip watering of trees, shrubs, perennials and vegetables also limited to those hours. Beginning Oct. 1, 2026, all lawn watering and lawn spray irrigation is prohibited in the district.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 rules; lawn-watering ban from Oct. 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Wheat Ridge Water District says it will not grant any variance for planting seed or sod during the drought and discourages new sod and seed installations, since customers may water only on assigned days.

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Customers of Wheat Ridge Water District (a Denver Water qualifying provider) can get up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 eligible rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain) that replace existing heads; one rebate per residence per 10 years, applied for online within 90 days of purchase and subject to available funds.

permit_office.name: Town of Morrison Building Department (contracted to Charles Abbott Associates, Inc.)
permit_office.summary: Morrison contracts with Charles Abbott Associates to enforce Town codes; permits are applied for through the Town's online Building Permit Application, and inspection requests are due by 4 p.m. the business day before (building@morrisonco.us).

row_permit.summary: Work in Morrison's public right-of-way needs a separate Work in Public Right of Way Permit (form revised July 2026, showing a $250 fee and $200 development review deposit), with a site/work plan, an MUTCD traffic control plan when access is affected, and a $1,000,000 general liability certificate naming the Town as additional insured. The permit holder must post security equal to 100% of estimated restoration cost, warranty restoration for one year, get Colorado 811 locates before excavating, and arrange inspections with the Public Works Director.

water_provider.name: Town of Morrison Public Works (water and sewer utility)
water_provider.summary: Morrison's raw water comes from Bear Creek and is treated at the Town's membrane filtration plant.

other.summary: Morrison's code enforcement and building inspections are provided through Charles Abbott Associates, and the Building Department posts a separate Fence Permit Application.

water_provider.name: Wheat Ridge Water District
water_provider.summary: The district, which buys its water from Denver Water, lists Mountain View in its service area.

watering_rules.summary: Wheat Ridge Water District is a Denver Water distributor and says Denver Water's Stage 1 drought and watering rules apply to it: lawn watering only on two assigned days a week (by even, odd or other address type) and only before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m., with hand or drip watering of trees, shrubs, perennials and vegetables also limited to those hours. Beginning Oct. 1, 2026, all lawn watering and lawn spray irrigation is prohibited in the district.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 rules; lawn-watering ban from Oct. 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Wheat Ridge Water District says it will not grant any variance for planting seed or sod during the drought and discourages new sod and seed installations, since customers may water only on assigned days.

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Customers of Wheat Ridge Water District (a Denver Water qualifying provider) can get up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 eligible rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain) that replace existing heads; one rebate per residence per 10 years, applied for online within 90 days of purchase and subject to available funds.

permit_office.name: City of Aurora Building Division (Building Permit Center, 303.739.7420)

row_permit.summary: Work in Aurora's public right-of-way requires a Public Improvement Permit from the Development Services Permit Center (pipermits@auroragov.org, 303.739.7420). Any permit that affects traffic, bicyclists or pedestrians, including sidewalk repair or replacement and street cuts, needs an approved traffic control plan before the permit is issued.

flatwork_permit.summary: Aurora's DIY home-improvement handbook says a concrete patio needs no permit unless it is more than 30 inches above grade, while driveways and sidewalks need a permit with a public improvement inspection. Replacing a driveway like-for-like needs no permit; a new or expanded driveway needs a plot plan reviewed by the Engineering and Zoning divisions.

retaining_wall.summary: Aurora's DIY handbook lists retaining walls as requiring a building permit with plan submittal and a structural inspection (no height exemption is given) and landscape walls as requiring a permit with a public improvement inspection. Landscaping alone needs no permit unless retaining walls are installed or the site is regraded.

water_provider.name: Aurora Water (City of Aurora)

watering_rules.summary: Aurora has been in a Stage 1 drought since April 6, 2026: non-drip irrigation is limited to two assigned days per week, with no watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. (May 1-Sept. 30), and a run that continues past midnight counts as two days. A Sept. 28, 2026 ordinance bans spray irrigation Oct. 1-April 30 (Oct. 15-April 30 for residential yards, parks and athletic fields), so homes on residential meters must stop irrigating by Oct. 15.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 declared Apr. 6, 2026; seasonal spray-irrigation ban adopted Sept. 28, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Installing or replacing sod or seed, or installing or renovating a sprinkler system, requires an Aurora Water lawn, seed and irrigation permit and inspection ($42.75 residential in 2026); the permit exempts new sod from watering restrictions for 20 days and new seed for 30 days. During Stage 1 only low-water grasses (e.g., buffalograss, Dog Tuff or Tahoma 31 bermudagrass, native seed) may be installed, and the Sept. 28, 2026 ordinance prohibits new cool-season turf such as Kentucky bluegrass and fescue citywide.
