rebates.summary: Pays $3 per sq ft to convert existing irrigated, well-maintained lawn to a water-wise landscape, or $0.50 per sq ft for native or low-water grass; projects must be pre-approved (no retroactive rebates). The 2026 fall application window runs Nov. 1, 2026 to Jan. 1, 2027, with completion due July 31, 2027.

For upgrades to existing systems (new systems do not qualify): smart controllers $200 (one per household per 10 years), rain sensors $15 wired/$50 wireless, soil moisture sensors $100 each (max two), check-valve rotors $12, pressure-regulating pop-up bodies $9 and high-efficiency nozzles $6 each (up to 50 of each), and spray-to-drip conversion $75 per zone (up to three zones).
Free professional water-wise landscape designs (design area up to 2,500 sq ft) for Aurora Water customers, handled remotely by phone, email and aerial mapping.

backflow.summary: Aurora City Code Sec. 138-170 requires any required backflow prevention assembly (Aurora Water names irrigation systems among the connections that need one) to be tested by a certified backflow technician at installation and at least annually, with results submitted online through Aurora Water's backflow portal before the due date. The property owner is ultimately responsible.

other.summary: Aurora's DIY handbook limits front yards to no more than 40% concrete and requires driveways to be at least 3 feet from the property line.

Before a lawn permit is issued, turf areas must be amended with at least 4 cubic yards of compost per 1,000 sq ft, tilled 6 inches deep; during Stage 1 the online permit portal is disabled and lawn permits are requested by email to Aurora Water Conservation (303.739.7195).
Aurora allows artificial turf up to a 50% coverage maximum (it is not rebated), and above-ground spray-head irrigation systems are not permitted.

permit_office.name: City of Centennial Building Division (303-754-3321)

row_permit.summary: Centennial Public Works requires a Right-of-Way permit for all construction in or occupation of city right-of-way, applied for through the city's online self-service portal. Contractors must be licensed and bonded with the City, and work must follow Centennial's Right-of-Way Regulations.

water_provider.name: Several providers: Denver Water distributors and East Cherry Creek Valley Water & Sanitation District (ECCV)
water_provider.notes: The City says much of Centennial's water comes through Denver Water distributors and points residents to its Property Search to identify the district serving an address; ECCV serves the eastern portion of Centennial.

watering_rules.summary: Rules depend on the water provider. Homes supplied through Denver Water follow its 2026 Stage 1 drought rules (single-family lawns two days a week, even addresses Sunday/Thursday and odd addresses Wednesday/Saturday, only 6 p.m.-10 a.m.; no lawn or spray watering since Oct. 1, 2026), while ECCV has banned lawn watering since Oct. 1, 2026 and allows trees, shrubs and gardens to be watered only on specific days.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Denver Water Stage 1 from Mar. 25, 2026; ECCV fall/winter restrictions from Oct. 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: For Denver Water-supplied homes: Denver Water stopped issuing watering establishment permits for new seed, sod or plants on Oct. 1, 2026, except for Lead Replacement Program, mainline pipe replacement and Certificate of Occupancy projects; establishing grass after Sept. 30 otherwise is not allowed, and watering grass outside a permit can bring fines of up to $2,000.

rebates.summary: For ECCV service-area customers: rain sensors up to $25 wired/$50 wireless, $5 per pressure-regulating spray body or check-valve rotor (up to 25), $2.50 per high-efficiency nozzle (up to 25), and 50% up to $100 for a weather-based smart controller.
ECCV offers a limited number of turf replacement (Lawn Replacement) discounts, discounted Garden In A Box kits and free sprinkler audits through Resource Central.

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 qualifying rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain), once per residence every 10 years; replacements only (not new construction), applied for online within 90 days of purchase. Available to customers billed by Denver Water or a listed qualifying provider.

backflow.summary: Centennial requires a one-stop 'Irrigation Line' permit to install a new backflow preventer. Testing is not covered on the city's site; Denver Water, for example, requires irrigation backflow assemblies to be tested at installation and annually by a certified tester and reported to its Cross-Connection Control office.

other.summary: Grading, erosion and sediment control permits in Centennial are issued by the Southeast Metro Stormwater Authority (SEMSWA), not the city.

Centennial's Building Division refers residents to 2021 IRC Section R105 ('work exempt from permit') to judge whether a project needs a building permit; the city's 2023 code adoption (Ordinance 2023-O-06) deleted only the IRC's deck exemption.
All contractors and subcontractors must be licensed with the City of Centennial; homeowners may pull a permit only for work they do themselves on a home they occupy.
A permit is required for all new fences and for replacement of existing fences.

permit_office.name: City of Englewood Building Division (permits through the city's IMS portal)

row_permit.summary: Englewood Public Works requires a Concrete Permit to remove or install any curb and gutter, sidewalk or concrete alley; it requires a Class D6 contractor license from the Building Division, a certificate of insurance naming the City and a performance bond. Applications go through the city's IMS portal, and inspections must be scheduled at least 24 hours before construction.

water_provider.name: City of Englewood Utilities Department (303-762-2635)

watering_rules.summary: Englewood Utilities says no mandatory restrictions are in place and asks customers to voluntarily water no more than three days a week (odd addresses Monday, Wednesday, Friday; even addresses Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday) and only before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m. It says any mandatory restrictions would be announced on its website.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated page describing 'this summer' (checked Oct. 13, 2026)

rebates.program: Lawn Replacement Program (City of Englewood with Resource Central)
rebates.summary: In 2026, residents could replace up to 425 sq ft of turf with a low-water landscape for $1 per sq ft; applications opened March 9, 2026.
Listed by the City as a city program for installing drought-tolerant garden kits; the city page gives no 2026 pricing.

rebates.program: Free Energy & Water Services (Mile High Youth Corps)
rebates.summary: Listed by the City as a non-city program offering free energy and water assessments for qualifying households.

other.summary: Englewood Public Works directs all utility locate requests to the Utility Notification Center of Colorado: dial 811 or 800-922-1987.

permit_office.name: City of Littleton Permit Center / Building Division (eTRAKiT portal, 303-795-3751)

row_permit.summary: Littleton requires a Right-of-Way permit for any work or equipment occupying the public right-of-way, including sidewalks and alleys (City Code 8-1-3); contractors must be licensed with the City and provide bonds and insurance, and applications go through eTRAKiT with a traffic control plan and pre-construction photos. Work without a required permit carries a $250 first-offense fee.

flatwork_permit.summary: Littleton's 'Do I Need A Permit?' guide says qualifying sidewalks and driveways that are no more than 30 inches above grade, not over a basement or story below and not part of an accessible route are exempt from a building permit; planning, floodplain or right-of-way approvals may still apply.

retaining_wall.summary: A retaining wall supporting no more than 4 vertical feet of cut or unbalanced fill may be exempt from a building permit if it meets the city's other exemption conditions (overall wall height and use limits); a surcharge on the wall removes the exemption, and zoning review for setbacks, easements and drainage may still apply.

water_provider.name: Denver Water
water_provider.notes: Littleton says all city residents are served by Denver Water; Denver Water lists the City of Littleton as a Total Service distributor.

watering_rules.summary: Denver Water declared a Stage 1 drought on March 25, 2026 (in effect through April 30, 2027 or until further notice): single-family homes could water lawns no more than two days a week (even-numbered addresses Sunday and Thursday, odd-numbered Wednesday and Saturday; all other properties Tuesday and Friday) and only between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m. Since Oct. 1, 2026, all lawn watering and spray irrigation are prohibited until further board action; trees, shrubs and gardens may still be watered with a hand-held hose with shut-off nozzle or drip.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Denver Water Stage 1 drought declared Mar. 25, 2026; lawn and spray-irrigation ban effective Oct. 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Denver Water stopped issuing watering establishment permits for new seed, sod or plants on Oct. 1, 2026, except for Lead Replacement Program, mainline pipe replacement and Certificate of Occupancy projects; establishing grass after Sept. 30 otherwise is not allowed, and watering grass outside a permit can bring fines of up to $2,000.

rebates.program: City of Littleton Lawn Replacement discount (via Resource Central)
rebates.summary: $750 off Resource Central's Lawn Replacement Program when at least one 200-sq-ft section of lawn is removed; Littleton residents qualify regardless of water provider, new projects only, one discount per project, limited spots.

rebates.program: City of Littleton Garden In A Box discount
rebates.summary: Littleton residents can get a $25 discount on Resource Central Garden In A Box kits (one discount per project).

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 qualifying rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain), once per residence every 10 years; replacements only (not new construction), applied for online within 90 days of purchase.

backflow.summary: Denver Water requires an approved backflow assembly on irrigation services (a pressure vacuum breaker or reduced-pressure assembly; atmospheric vacuum breakers and double checks are not allowed for irrigation), with single-family requirements assessed by site hazard. Assemblies must be tested at installation and annually by a certified tester during the May-September irrigation season, with reports sent to Denver Water's Cross-Connection Control office (crossconnectioncontrol@denverwater.org).

other.summary: A Littleton grading permit is required when the disturbed area exceeds 5,000 sq ft or 50 cubic yards, with engineer-stamped civil and drainage documents.

permit_office.name: City of Sheridan Building Department (Permit Technician 303-438-3302)

row_permit.summary: Work in Sheridan's right-of-way needs a Public Works Right of Way application submitted through the city's Electronic Plan Review (ePlan) portal. The city currently issues right-of-way permits only to contractors who verify that asphalt restoration will occur within 24 hours of a street cut.

water_provider.name: Denver Water
water_provider.notes: Denver Water lists the City of Sheridan as a Total Service distributor (Denver Water owns, operates and bills the system).

rebates.summary: A limited number of $25 discounts on water-wise Garden In A Box plant kits for Denver Water residential customers during the spring and fall sales.

other.summary: Sheridan's permit page lists a Plumbing/Mechanical/Landscaping permit application as required for all new installations or replacements; these over-the-counter permits must be paid in full (Permit Technician 303-438-3302).
CDOT, not the city, maintains US-285, Federal Boulevard and Santa Fe Drive and their rights-of-way within Sheridan.

permit_office.name: City of Glendale Building & Permits Department

row_permit.summary: Work in Glendale's right-of-way needs a Public Works Right of Way permit (2026 application online or as a PDF), emailed to PWpermits@glendale.co.us (303-639-4500).

water_provider.name: City of Glendale water utility (Public Works), supplied by Denver Water
water_provider.notes: Glendale buys all its water from Denver Water under a master-meter contract; the City maintains the water mains and bills customers.

watering_rules.summary: To align with Denver Water's 2026 drought response, Glendale requires multifamily, commercial and HOA properties to water only on Tuesdays and Fridays, and raised water rates 5% from May 1 until further notice.
watering_rules.as_of: Posted April 15, 2026

rebates.program: Denver Water rotary/high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle rebate
rebates.summary: Up to $3 per nozzle for 10 to 100 qualifying rotary nozzles (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain), once per residence every 10 years; replacements only (not new construction), applied for online within 90 days of purchase. The City of Glendale is on Denver Water's list of qualifying providers.

backflow.summary: Glendale and Denver Water require a backflow device on every water service in Glendale (irrigation typically needs a pressure vacuum breaker or reduced-pressure assembly), installed under city inspection. Devices must be tested annually by a certified technician at the owner's expense, with the report sent to Glendale Public Works (601 S. Elm St.) and records kept three years; failed tests must be reported immediately (303-639-4500).

other.summary: Glendale repairs water mains and meters, but repairs to taps, valves, fire lines and service lines are the property owner's responsibility.
All contractors, including those licensed in Denver, need a City of Glendale contractor license to pull a permit.

permit_office.name: City of Cherry Hills Village Building Division (Community Development, online permit portal)

row_permit.summary: Driveway work in the right-of-way (removal, replacement, overlay, new or relocated) needs a ROW Driveway permit ($150 fee, $5,000 two-year bond, $1 million liability insurance); new or relocated driveways that cut curb and gutter or valley pans or cross a bar ditch need a ROW Street Cut permit ($500 per cut). Permits are applied for through the city's online portal.

flatwork_permit.summary: Any addition or removal of impervious surface, such as a driveway or patio, requires a permit. If added impervious surface totals more than 2,500 sq ft (cumulative with past additions), a Phase III Drainage Plan is required, plus an as-built survey, engineer's letter and recorded maintenance agreement before the permit closes.

retaining_wall.summary: All fences and walls require a permit (walls over 6 ft or with a gate also get Building Code and/or South Metro Fire review). Outside a building envelope, retaining walls (tiers combined) may be no taller than 6 ft; walls over 6 ft must be tiered with no tier over 6 ft and tiers set back 1 ft per 2 ft of the higher tier's height, and a wall whose exposed side faces a street or neighboring property must be set back from the lot line at least 4/3 of its height.

water_provider.name: Denver Water (Total Service Agreement) plus several small districts
water_provider.notes: The City has a Total Service Agreement with Denver Water for the majority of residences; other parts of the City are served by districts including Southgate Water and Sanitation District, Englewood Utilities, Cherrymoor Water District, Hillcrest and Mansfield Heights Water and Sanitation Districts, and South University Place Water District (see the City's water district map and list).

Landscape work in the right-of-way (sod, irrigation, rock, wood chips, shrubs, trees) needs a ROW Landscape permit ($150, $5,000 two-year bond, $1 million insurance), and landscape materials and equipment may not be staged on city streets.

No residential lot may have more than two driveways per street frontage (three curb cuts total on corner or multi-frontage lots), and new or altered curb cuts for construction need Public Works approval before a building permit is issued.

permit_office.name: City of Greenwood Village Community Development - Building Permits & Inspections (303-486-5783)

row_permit.summary: Construction work in the Village right-of-way, including streets and sidewalks, goes through the Village's right-of-way permit process (application, review and inspection) via its online ROW permit portal; a ROW bond template and the Public Infrastructure Design and Construction Standards apply.

flatwork_permit.summary: A Flatwork Permit ($50) is required to install or replace more than 100 sq ft of impervious area, such as sidewalks or driveways; apply through the Online Access Portal.

water_provider.name: Several water districts, including Denver Water (City of Greenwood Village Total Service area)
water_provider.notes: The Village directs residents to its Water Districts map to find which provider serves a home; Denver Water lists the City of Greenwood Village as a Total Service distributor, and the Village map credits Southgate Water District and Castlewood Water and Sanitation District as data sources.

The Village lists landscaping, fences, and concrete or asphalt work over 100 sq ft among residential projects that require a permit.

permit_office.name: Town of Bow Mar Building Department (run from the Columbine Valley Town Hall office, 2 Middlefield Rd.)
permit_office.summary: Bow Mar's building plans, building permits and contractor licensing are administered through the Building Department office at Columbine Valley Town Hall (303-795-2063). Design Review Board approval is required before a building permit for work the board reviews.

row_permit.summary: A Street Cut/Driveway Permit from the Public Works Commissioner is required for any road cut, for building or replacing a driveway entrance to a Town road, and for driveway repairs that involve a culvert or drainage; a separate Right-of-Way Permit application is also posted, and processing can take up to 20 days. The 2024 form lists a $400 permit fee plus a $200 minimum inspection fee and engineering fees, a $5,000 one-year performance bond, a 2-year warranty on right-of-way work, a Town-approved traffic control plan and a Town Engineer inspection before fill.

flatwork_permit.summary: Bow Mar's Design Guidelines require Design Review Board approval for all patio projects, even at grade, and patios must sit inside the lot's building envelope. Town Code Chapter 11 requires a permit to construct or replace a driveway.

water_provider.name: Bow Mar Water and Sanitation District (Denver Water distributor)
water_provider.summary: The district distributes water to 296 residences in western Arapahoe and eastern Jefferson counties, points customers to Denver Water's water quality reports, and is obligated by contract to enforce Denver Water's water use restrictions.

watering_rules.summary: The district adopted Denver Water's 2026 Stage 1 drought rules: two assigned days a week (even addresses Sun/Thu, odd Wed/Sat, multifamily and commercial Tue/Fri) with watering only from 6 p.m. to 10 a.m. Under District Resolution 2026-9-1, all grass watering and spray irrigation are prohibited after Sept. 30, 2026 until further notice (trees, shrubs and perennials may still be hand-watered or drip-irrigated), and single-family violations bring a warning, then $250, $500 and $1,000 fines.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Aug. 12, 2026 notice; grass-watering ban from Oct. 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Resolution 2026-9-1 allows no grass establishment after Sept. 30, 2026 except under special circumstances through an approved variance. The district's pages do not describe a sod permit for the regular season.

rebates.summary: Bow-Mar W&S District is on Denver Water's list of qualifying providers, so its customers can claim up to $3 per rotary or high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle (10 to 100 nozzles, once per residence per 10 years).

backflow.summary: Since 2025 the Bow Mar Water and Sanitation District, not Denver Water, has run the backflow prevention and cross-connection control program, and backflow test reports go to the district at info@bowmarwater.org. The district's page does not state a testing frequency.

other.summary: Design Review Board approval is required for landscaping that could affect neighbors' views or substantially alter existing landscaping, and for grade changes, including berms, that disturb more than 4 cubic yards of soil. Comparable replacement trees do not need approval.
Fences need Design Review Board approval plus a building permit and are limited to 5 feet; chain-link, vinyl/plastic and front-yard fences are prohibited.
Contractors working on permitted projects must hold a Town of Bow Mar contractor license.

permit_office.name: Town of Columbine Valley Building Department
permit_office.summary: The Town issues residential building permits from Town Hall, 2 Middlefield Rd. (303-795-1434), with applications filed through its GovPilot portal and inspections by contracted inspectors. Every contractor and subcontractor on a permit must hold a Town contractor license, and exterior changes need HOA approval.

row_permit.summary: Work in the Town right-of-way, and any permanent private use of it, requires a Street Cut and Right of Way Permit under the Town's Rights of Way ordinance (Code Ch. 12.13), applied for through GovPilot.

water_provider.name: Denver Water
water_provider.summary: The Town lists Denver Water as the water provider (general 303-893-2444) and Platte Canyon Water & Sanitation as the sewer provider.

watering_rules.summary: Under Denver Water's Stage 1 drought (declared Mar. 25, 2026), lawns could be watered on two assigned days a week (single-family even addresses Sun/Thu, odd Wed/Sat; multifamily, commercial, HOA and government Tue/Fri) and never from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Since Oct. 1, 2026 all lawn watering and spray irrigation are prohibited until further Board action (trees, shrubs and perennials may be hand-watered with a shutoff nozzle or drip-irrigated any day), with single-family fines of $500, then $1,000.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (Stage 1 from Mar. 25, 2026; lawn-watering ban from Oct. 1, 2026)

new_sod.summary: Denver Water's watering establishment permit allowed extra watering for new seed or sod (up to 3 weeks; 8 weeks for native grass seed), but as of Oct. 1, 2026 it is issued only for Lead Replacement Program, mainline pipe replacement or Certificate of Occupancy projects. Other grass establishment after Sept. 30, 2026 requires an approved variance.

rebates.summary: Up to $3 per rotary or high-efficiency sprinkler nozzle (Hunter MP, Rain Bird, Toro Precision, K-Rain) for 10 to 100 nozzles, once per residence per 10 years, while funds last.

rebates.program: Turfgrass removal discount (Denver Water with Resource Central)
rebates.summary: An upfront discount of up to $750 on turf removal services; Denver Water says all 2026 discounts have been allocated.

backflow.summary: Denver Water requires backflow assemblies, including those on irrigation services, to be tested by a certified tester at installation and annually, with irrigation assemblies tested when the water is turned on for the May–September season. Reports go to crossconnectioncontrol@denverwater.org, and a $250 penalty applies if three mailed notices go unanswered and the account enters suspension.

other.summary: The Town right-of-way generally extends about 3 feet past the edge of the gutter pan; residents may landscape it but it stays public property, plantings must not block sightlines, and a 3-foot clear radius must be kept around fire hydrants.
The Town and utilities are not responsible for damage to irrigation lines, invisible dog fences or other private features in the right-of-way during maintenance, utility work or snow removal.

permit_office.name: SAFEbuilt (building permits for the Town of Foxfield)
permit_office.summary: Foxfield's building permits are issued by SAFEbuilt through the Community Connect online portal (building official 303-941-4429), with zoning review by SAFEbuilt Studio and engineering review by the Town engineer, SEH. The Town does not require contractor licensing.

row_permit.summary: New driveways, culverts and temporary construction driveways need a Residential Driveway and Culvert Right-of-Way Use Permit reviewed by the Town Engineer ($250 fee plus a $500 engineering review deposit where applicable; 12–22 ft wide; culvert size set by the Town Engineer), and other work in the Town right-of-way needs a separate Right-of-Way permit. No permit is needed for improvements to the part of an existing driveway on private property.

flatwork_permit.summary: The Town lists concrete flatwork outside the Town right-of-way among projects that do not require a permit.

retaining_wall.summary: Retaining walls over 4 feet, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, need a building permit and engineering review, and the Town engineer (SEH) reviews all retaining walls regardless of height.

water_provider.name: Private wells (most homes); Arapahoe County Water & Wastewater Authority (ACWWA) central water available
water_provider.summary: Most Foxfield homes have private wells permitted by the State Engineer; a property can connect to ACWWA by buying a water tap ($32,228 in 2024) and transferring its deep water rights. All homes are on septic.

watering_rules.summary: The Town publishes no outdoor watering schedule; each private well's allowed uses and limits depend on its State Engineer permit, which owners can check with the Colorado Division of Water Resources (303-866-3581) or its well permit search.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated Town page (accessed 2026-10-13)

other.summary: Residents are responsible for keeping their driveway culverts clear and repaired; clearing debris needs no permit, but repairs involving excavation or replacement need a right-of-way permit.
Lawn sprinkler installation is a One-Stop permit, and fences need a building permit (solid fences that may change drainage also get SEH engineering review).

permit_office.name: Town of Deer Trail (Town Clerk)
permit_office.summary: Building permits are applied for through the Town's online Building Permit Application; the Town quotes the fee after processing, adds a flat $25 administrative fee (Ordinance 238) and sends a permit to post at the work site (Town Hall 303-769-4464).

water_provider.name: Town of Deer Trail Water & Sewer
water_provider.summary: The Town provides water and sewer service (rates effective with January 2026 billing) and publishes the drinking water quality reports; Ordinance 205 (1999) brings the Denver Basin groundwater under the town into its municipal water plan.

watering_rules.summary: No current watering schedule is posted; under Ordinance 190 the Town Board may restrict or prohibit lawn sprinkling by resolution after newspaper notice, hoses must have a nozzle or sprinkler attached, and sprinklers may not be set to interfere with sidewalk traffic.
watering_rules.as_of: Ordinance 190, effective Aug. 1, 1996

other.summary: The Town has a separate online Fence Permit Application.
Ordinance 205 prohibits new private wells into the Denver Basin aquifers within town limits; existing permitted wells are not affected.

permit_office.name: Town of Parker Building Division (Community Development)
permit_office.summary: The Building Division handles all building permits and inspections within incorporated Parker; applications go through the eTRAKiT portal, and contractors must call the office to set up an account and licensing (303-841-1970).

row_permit.summary: Right-of-Way Use Permits from the Engineering/Public Works Department are required for all construction or alteration in the Town's public right-of-way and are applied for in eTRAKiT, where contractors must register. The checklist requires a project narrative, a certificate of insurance naming the Town, an MUTCD traffic control plan and a concrete or asphalt mix design as applicable, and restoration must be finished within five days of completing the work.

retaining_wall.summary: A building permit is required for retaining or block walls over 48 inches tall.

water_provider.name: Parker Water & Sanitation District (most of town); some subdivisions served by Cottonwood Water, Pinery Water and Wastewater, Stonegate, Compark or Meridian
water_provider.summary: PWSD serves most of the Town of Parker, but depending on the subdivision a home may be served by one of five other districts; PWSD's service-area map or customer care (303-841-4627) confirms an address.

watering_rules.summary: PWSD's summer restrictions prohibit watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. and any water waste, and its watering-day guidelines assign Sun/Tue/Thu to even addresses and Mon/Wed/Sat to odd addresses and to multifamily, HOA and commercial properties. PWSD says the daytime restrictions ended for the year on Oct. 1; customers of the other districts follow their own district's rules.
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season (PWSD page notes restrictions ended Oct. 1)

new_sod.summary: During the restriction season PWSD customers need a sod/seed establishment permit (online form) to water new sod or seed outside the standard guidelines; PWSD says permits are no longer required after Oct. 1, when daytime restrictions end.

rebates.summary: For current PWSD customers (property owners): $50 for a WaterSense smart controller, up to $5 per rotary nozzle (max $100 per home), 50% of a rain sensor's cost up to $50, and up to $75 for converting a full sprinkler zone to drip; first-come, first-served until the year's funds run out.

rebates.program: Turf removal discount (Resource Central / South Metro Water Supply Authority)
rebates.summary: PWSD customers can get a $750 turf removal discount through Resource Central's Lawn Replacement program, first-come, first-served until the year's funds are exhausted.
A limited number of $25 discounts on Resource Central Garden In A Box water-wise garden kits for PWSD customers each year.
Free sprinkler system consultations by Resource Central technicians for PWSD customers, ending with a custom watering schedule; first-come, first-served while funding lasts.

backflow.summary: PWSD's Cross-Connection Control Manual (Apr. 21, 2026 update) requires irrigation backflow preventers to be tested at seasonal startup and new assemblies within 10 days of installation, with results submitted within 10 days by an ABPA- or ASSE-certified tester through PWSD's backflow tester portal. Reduced-pressure assemblies are required on dedicated irrigation, commercial and 4-plus-unit multifamily services, and single-family homes are evaluated by degree of hazard.

other.summary: A Street Occupancy Permit is required to place landscape materials, storage containers, dumpsters or construction trailers in the Town right-of-way for more than 24 hours.

Altering a fence, changing landscaping, removing trees, altering the tree lawn or installing xeric landscaping may need Town approval; the Town says to check with Community Development (303-841-2332). Fences over 6 feet need a building permit.
Trees in the right-of-way are maintained by the HOA or metro district or, in some cases, the homeowner.

permit_office.name: Town of Castle Rock Development Services, Building Division (Building Counter)
permit_office.summary: Building permits are applied for and inspections scheduled through the Town's eTRAKiT portal (Building Counter: buildingcounter@crgov.com, 720-733-3527), and the Town's FAQ says to email the Building Counter with a project description to learn which permits are needed. The Town enforces the 2024 ICC codes for permit applications submitted on or after June 30, 2026.

water_provider.name: Castle Rock Water (Town of Castle Rock water utility)
water_provider.summary: Castle Rock Water (175 Kellogg Court, 720-733-6000) provides water service and runs the CRconserve.com conservation site.

watering_rules.summary: Castle Rock Water's mandatory residential schedule runs May 1–Sept. 30: water every third day only before 8 a.m. or after 8 p.m., on days set by the last digit of the address (0–3 square, 4–6 circle, 7–9 diamond), while nonresidential properties water three days a week from midnight to 8 a.m. (west of I-25 Mon/Wed/Fri, east Tue/Thu/Sat). The schedule is not currently in effect, but a Drought Stage 1 advisory asks all customers to cut use 10% voluntarily, and repeat residential violations bring $25, $50, $100 and then $200 surcharges after a first warning.
watering_rules.as_of: Undated pages accessed 2026-10-13 (schedule season May 1–Sept. 30)

new_sod.summary: A $9 temporary watering exemption, which can be requested the day of installation, lets new sod be watered any day for 21 days and new seed or plants for 30 days, still only before 8 a.m. or after 8 p.m.; exemptions are not issued in July. Per the Town FAQ (updated Dec. 27, 2023), Kentucky bluegrass has been banned from new development since 2018, and new homes may not have front-yard turf, with limits on back-yard turf.

rebates.summary: $3.25 per sq ft ($1.00 per sq ft for hardscape) for replacing at least 400 sq ft, or a whole front yard, of healthy high-water turf, up to 1,500 sq ft, with a pre-approved application and initial inspection; artificial turf does not qualify. The 2026 program is closed, and 2027 details are due in April 2027.
Up to $5 per rotary nozzle that replaces a fixed-spray nozzle; equipment must be bought and installed and the application filed in the same rebate year.
Castle Rock Water customers may qualify for a $25 discount on Resource Central Garden In A Box xeric garden kits.

backflow.summary: The Town's Landscape and Irrigation Criteria Manual (Apr. 23, 2026) requires a passing backflow prevention assembly test within 10 days of irrigation system start-up each season and before a certificate of occupancy; the manual does not say where test reports are filed.

other.summary: Castle Rock Water requires rain sensors on all irrigation systems.
Hand watering (hose held in hand) is allowed any day and time, and irrigation maintenance may run any time while a person is actively attending it.

permit_office.name: City of Castle Pines Building Department
permit_office.summary: The City issues building permits (applied for online through CommunityCore or on a paper application) and City staff perform inspections (303-705-0227, buildingdept@castlepinesco.gov); permits are valid 180 days.

row_permit.summary: Right-of-way permits are Public Works permits applied for through the City's SmartGov portal, with checklists and bonding requirements in SmartGov's Resources tab and a Right-of-Way Permit Bond Form on the City site. The 2026 fee schedule lists ROW fees such as an $82 base fee plus per-linear-foot charges for sidewalk and curb-and-gutter work, $8.75 per sq ft for paved street cuts and $375 for a 90-day dumpster placement.

water_provider.name: Castle Pines North Metropolitan District (west of I-25); Parker Water & Sanitation District (east of I-25)
water_provider.summary: The City says Castle Pines North Metropolitan District provides water and sewer to all residents and businesses west of I-25, and Parker Water & Sanitation District serves those east of I-25.

watering_rules.summary: CPNMD's 2026 schedule allows watering three days a week, May through September, only after 8 p.m. and before 8 a.m. on assigned days (even addresses Sun/Tue/Thu, odd Mon/Wed/Sat, multifamily and commercial Mon/Wed/Fri); drip irrigation is allowed any time and water waste is prohibited. Homes east of I-25 follow PWSD's rules (no watering 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; even Sun/Tue/Thu, odd Mon/Wed/Sat).
watering_rules.as_of: 2026 season

new_sod.summary: CPNMD customers may water new sod or plants daily under a 21-day exemption, avoiding 8 a.m.–8 p.m., and establishment is not permitted in July or August. PWSD customers east of I-25 need a PWSD sod/seed establishment permit during its restriction season.

rebates.summary: Up to $3 per sq ft for residential lawn replacement (up to $2.50 for commercial/HOA); pre-approval of designs is strongly encouraged, and designs must include roughly 50% ColoradoScape plants.
$100 for a WaterSense-labeled smart controller, limit one per residential customer; rebates must be filed in the same calendar year.
$5 per nozzle for replacement rotator nozzles.
$25 off a Resource Central Garden In A Box kit when Castle Pines North Metropolitan District is selected at checkout, while supplies last.
PWSD customers can use PWSD's smart controller, rotary nozzle, rain sensor and spray-to-drip rebates, and $750 Resource Central turf removal discounts.

backflow.summary: CPNMD requires annual testing by a certified technician of backflow devices on non-single-family properties (commercial buildings, HOAs, irrigation systems and fire suppression systems) and on single-family homes with a backflow device on a fire sprinkler system; it uses contractor BackFlow Secure, charges $12.50 a month per eligible account and set a March 31, 2026 deadline. PWSD's program applies east of I-25.

other.summary: Contractors must hold a City contractor license before working, and no permits are issued for unregistered contractors; classes include concrete and form ($75/yr), excavating including cuts into the right-of-way ($75/yr), asphalt paving ($75/yr) and single trades such as landscaping and lawn sprinkler systems ($50/yr).
Installing a lawn sprinkler system requires a 1-Stop building permit, and fences over 7 feet need a plan-review permit.

permit_office.name: City of Lone Tree Building Division
permit_office.summary: The City's Building Division issues building permits, which are accepted only electronically through the Accela portal (720-390-5211, building@cityoflonetree.com).

row_permit.summary: Right-of-Way, Access and GESC permits are handled by Public Works through Accela, and a permit is required before any work affecting the public right-of-way; contractors need a certificate of liability insurance naming the City as additional insured. Permits generally issue within five working days, are valid six months, and inspections must be scheduled 24 hours ahead.

flatwork_permit.summary: The City lists concrete walks, patios and driveways among projects that typically do not require a building permit, but advises checking HOA and zoning rules first.

retaining_wall.summary: The City lists retaining walls under 4 feet among projects that typically do not need a building permit; the page does not address surcharged walls.

water_provider.name: Southgate Water and Sanitation District (west of I-25); Parker Water & Sanitation District (east of I-25); Northern Douglas County Water and Sanitation District (some Terra Ridge homes)
water_provider.summary: The City says residents get water from three districts by location: Southgate west of I-25 (follows Denver Water rules), PWSD east of I-25, and Northern Douglas County W&S District for some Terra Ridge homes along Indian Wells Drive (follows Highlands Ranch Water rules). The City itself does not set or enforce watering restrictions.

watering_rules.summary: As of April 1, 2026: Southgate customers followed Denver Water's Stage 1 rules (two days a week, even addresses Sun/Thu and odd Wed/Sat, watering only 6 p.m.–10 a.m.); PWSD customers watered three days a week (even Sun/Tue/Thu, odd Mon/Wed/Sat) but not 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; and Northern Douglas County customers two days a week (odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun) with no watering 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Denver Water has since prohibited watering any grass after Sept. 30, 2026 for everyone who receives its water, and PWSD's daytime restrictions ended Oct. 1.
watering_rules.as_of: April 1, 2026 (City summary); Denver Water grass-watering ban from Oct. 1, 2026

new_sod.summary: The City's water page gives no sod rules; PWSD customers need a PWSD sod/seed establishment permit during its restriction season, and under Denver Water's rules (which Southgate follows) grass establishment after Sept. 30, 2026 requires an approved variance.

rebates.program: PWSD Water Efficiency Rebates (PWSD customers, east of I-25)
rebates.summary: For current PWSD customers (property owners): $50 for a WaterSense smart controller, up to $5 per rotary nozzle (max $100 per home), 50% of a rain sensor's cost up to $50, and up to $75 for converting a full sprinkler zone to drip; first-come, first-served until the year's funds run out.

rebates.program: Turf removal discount (Resource Central / South Metro Water Supply Authority) (PWSD customers, east of I-25)
rebates.summary: PWSD customers can get a $750 turf removal discount through Resource Central's Lawn Replacement program, first-come, first-served until the year's funds are exhausted.

backflow.summary: For PWSD customers (east of I-25), irrigation backflow preventers must be tested at seasonal startup, with results submitted within 10 days by a certified tester through PWSD's portal. The City's pages do not cover backflow rules for the other districts.

other.summary: Dumpsters and portable toilets placed in the right-of-way need a Right-of-Way permit.
Fences under 7 feet typically do not need a building permit.

permit_office.name: Town of Larkspur Building Department (permits and inspections provided by SAFEbuilt)
permit_office.summary: For properties inside Larkspur town limits, building permits and inspections are provided by SAFEbuilt and issued through its CommunityCore site (Town Hall 303-681-2324); the Town posts a street list for checking whether an address is in town limits.

row_permit.summary: The Town's Public Works page posts a Right of Way Use Permit Application for work in the Town right-of-way, and the Town has adopted Douglas County's storm drainage and roadway design criteria (Ordinance 3.61).

water_provider.name: Town of Larkspur water and sewer
water_provider.summary: The Town bills water and sewer service, publishes the Town of Larkspur Water Quality Report and takes water emergency calls inside town limits (after hours: Semocor, 303-681-2253); it has adopted the Perry Park Water & Sanitation District rules and regulations (Resolution 12-06).

other.summary: The Building Department requires permits for all new construction and most building projects, and SAFEbuilt handles inspection scheduling (720-641-1956).
